| 11 | Verification and tool-call integrity | [SPEC-11](specs/SPEC-11-verification-and-tool-call-integrity.md) | [PLAN-11](plans/PLAN-11-verification-and-tool-call-integrity.md) | M1/M3 | AGT-112, 113, 114 |
| C1 | Contest (separate product; frozen until judging ends) | [SPEC-C1](specs/SPEC-C1-contest-submission-track.md) | [PLAN-C1](plans/PLAN-C1-contest-submission-track.md) | post-contest | — (not a client gate) |

## How to execute

0. If more than one agent (or person) will implement in parallel, read [CONCURRENCY.md](CONCURRENCY.md) first. It covers slice claims, worktrees, hot files, the gateway lock and merge order.
1. **Start with M0** (ROADMAP). Merge PLAN-08 PR-8a first, so that test runs stop writing into the real `~/.nexus`. Then land PLAN-06 PR-6a (version sync) and PLAN-09 PR-9a (ledger checker, historical banners, cheap doc fixes).
2. **M1 is the critical path.** Work through PLAN-01, PLAN-02, PLAN-03 and PLAN-11 PR-11a/b in the PR slices listed. Each plan names its safe change boundary, code locations, tests and rollback.
3. **For every PR:**
   - update the matching REQUIREMENTS rows (status, test reference, commit);
   - keep `scripts/check_requirements.mjs` green;
   - run `make test` on a snapshot copy, never while editing (tasks/lessons.md).
4. M2 and M4 run in parallel with M1/M3. Held-out task authoring (agent-authored, as authorised) and the standalone proxy start during M1.
5. Cut `v1.0.0-rc.1` only when G0–G4 pass. Then run ACCEPTANCE §4–§8 against the **installed** RC.

## Conventions

- **Requirement IDs.** `REQ-<AREA>-0xx` marks a commitment carried over from history. `REQ-<AREA>-1xx` marks a new v1 requirement.
- **Finding IDs.** These are owned by the scoped evidence files: AGT, VER, PRV, SEC, PER, TUI, REL, DX, MNT, HIST, EVL, CON, PERF, DOC.
- **Acceptance IDs.** `ACC-<AREA>-NN`. Each is defined in its spec, or in ACCEPTANCE §3.1.
- **Evidence labels.** SRC, TEST, RT, MEAS, DOC, HIST, INF, UNV (REQUIREMENTS §1).
- **Status ladder.** open → partial → implemented → tested → visually-accepted → product-qualified. Independent acceptance is recorded separately.

This package supersedes the Issue #12 matrices and the PHASE and WP documents as the source of current requirements. Those documents remain as historical record.

```sh
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

| File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
| `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
| `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
| `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/config.ts`, `security.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `plugins.ts` | 01, 03 | Claim required. PLAN-01 PR-1e and PLAN-03 must not run at the same time on `sandbox.ts` or `security.ts`. |
| `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts` | 01, 02 | **PLAN-01 PR-1a (effect classes) lands first.** PLAN-02 PR-2c adds schema fields afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tester.ts` | 01, 11 | **PLAN-01 PR-1c lands before PLAN-11 PR-11b/11c.** |
| `cli/src/core/state.ts` | 04, 08 | **PLAN-08 PR-8a (HOME isolation) lands before everything.** |
| `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs` | 01, 02, 06 | Claim required. The protocol version number is owned by PLAN-02 PR-2a. PLAN-06 PR-6c only reads it. |
| `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{live_state,live_view}.rs` | 01, 02 | Claim required |
| `package.json`, `cli/package.json`, `core/Cargo.toml`, lockfiles | 01, 06, 07, 08 | **Only one agent at a time.** Version fields are written only by `scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Dependency changes are separate commits that touch only the lockfile and manifest. |
| `harness.sh`, `install.sh`, `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `.github/workflows/*` | 05, 06, 07, 09, C1 | Claim required. Workflow edits are separate commits. |
| `cli/dist/**` | all, while tracked | Do not commit `cli/dist` from slices. PLAN-07 PR-7d untracks it (DEC-10). Until that merges, only the merging agent rebuilds and commits dist, in a final separate commit, after rebasing. |
| `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md`, `quickstart.md` | 05, 09 and doc tasks in every plan | Edit only the sections your slice changes. Hold a short `FILE_` claim. |

### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

## 5. Commit and merge discipline

1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.

## 6. Coordination records

| Record | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Claims | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` | Who owns which slice or file right now |
| Claim log | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims.log` (append-only, one line per event) | Claim, release, broken claim, boundary request |
| Boundary requests and discovered requirements | The PR description, under the heading `Needs from other slices`. Mirrored as one line in the claim log. | So the owning slice's agent can pick it up. Never fixed silently out of scope. |
| Slice evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/v1/<plan>-<slice>/` (new directory per slice) | No shared evidence files, so agents cannot overwrite each other's evidence |

## 7. Safe parallel lanes

The following groupings can run at the same time with no hot-file contention beyond §4 claims. They are listed by milestone.

| Phase | Parallel lanes |
|---|---|
| M0 | (a) PLAN-08 PR-8a, which must merge first. Then in parallel: (b) PLAN-06 PR-6a, (c) PLAN-09 PR-9a. |
| M1 | (a) PLAN-01 PR-1a → PR-1b → PR-1c (sequential, owns `capabilities.ts`, `agent.ts` dispatch). (b) PLAN-02 PR-2a (Rust only). (c) PLAN-03 PR-3a → PR-3b (config/egress). (d) PLAN-11 PR-11a (`parser.ts`) and PR-11b (`tester.ts`, after PR-1c). Lanes (b), (c) and (d) do not touch `capabilities.ts`. |
| M2 (alongside M1) | (a) PLAN-07 PR-7a/7b/7c (workflows, scripts). (b) PLAN-06 PR-6b after PLAN-01 PR-1b (shares `index.ts` flags). |
| M3 | (a) PLAN-04 (`agent.ts` turn, operation runner). (b) PLAN-05 (`client.ts`, provider modules). (c) PLAN-10 harness (`eval/`, no product files). (d) Held-out task authoring by the agent author, **outside the repository**: no access to Nexus source or the development set (DEC-05). |
| M4 (alongside M3) | PLAN-08 PR-8b..8e. Coordinate with PLAN-04 on `state.ts` through `FILE_` claims. |
| M5 | **Serial on `GATEWAY`.** The eval runner, the stripped-proxy runs and the independent reviewer's live task each take the `GATEWAY` claim. The terminal matrix (E3) and the install matrix (E2) can run in parallel with gateway runs. |

## 8. Independence constraints

- The held-out task author must not see Nexus source, the development tasks or tuning history. It runs in a separate session with only the task schema and external repositories. Its output is sealed by a sha256 manifest committed before RC1.
- The independent reviewer in ACCEPTANCE §8 must not be the agent or session that implemented the slices under review.
- An implementing agent never edits `eval/heldout-manifest.json`, scorer thresholds or ACCEPTANCE §6.4 after the freeze.

## How to execute

0. If more than one agent (or person) will implement in parallel, read [CONCURRENCY.md](CONCURRENCY.md) first. It covers slice claims, worktrees, hot files, the gateway lock and merge order.

2. **M1 is the critical path.** Work through PLAN-01, PLAN-02, PLAN-03 and PLAN-11 PR-11a/b in the PR slices listed. Each plan names its safe change boundary, code locations, tests and rollback.
3. **For every PR:**

   - keep `scripts/check_requirements.mjs` green;
   - run `make test` on a snapshot copy, never while editing (tasks/lessons.md).
4. M2 and M4 run in parallel with M1/M3. Held-out task authoring (agent-authored, as authorised) and the standalone proxy start during M1.

## Conventions

- **Requirement IDs.** `REQ-<AREA>-0xx` marks a commitment carried over from history. `REQ-<AREA>-1xx` marks a new v1 requirement.
- **Finding IDs.** These are owned by the scoped evidence files: AGT, VER, PRV, SEC, PER, TUI, REL, DX, MNT, HIST, EVL, CON, PERF, DOC.
- **Acceptance IDs.** `ACC-<AREA>-NN`. Each is defined in its spec, or in ACCEPTANCE §3.1.
- **Evidence labels.** SRC, TEST, RT, MEAS, DOC, HIST, INF, UNV (REQUIREMENTS §1).
- **Status ladder.** open → partial → implemented → tested → visually-accepted → product-qualified. Independent acceptance is recorded separately.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-agent-mail__fetch_inbox
entries.description:
Retrieve recent messages for an agent without mutating read/ack state.

Filters
-------
- `urgent_only`: only messages with importance in {high, urgent}
- `since_ts`: ISO-8601 timestamp string; messages strictly newer than this are returned
- `limit`: max number of messages (default 20)
- `include_bodies`: include full Markdown bodies in the payloads
- `topic`: filter to messages with this topic tag

Usage patterns
--------------
- Poll after each editing step in an agent loop to pick up coordination messages.
- Use `since_ts` with the timestamp from your last poll for efficient incremental fetches.
- Combine with `acknowledge_message` if `ack_required` is true.

Returns
-------
list[dict]
    Each message includes: { id, subject, from, created_ts, importance, ack_required, kind, [body_md] }

Example
-------
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"7","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"fetch_inbox","arguments":{
  "project_key":"/abs/path/backend","agent_name":"BlueLake","since_ts":"2025-10-23T00:00:00+00:00"
}}}
```

entries.name: mcp__mcp-agent-mail__search_messages
entries.description:
Full-text search over subject and body for a project.

Tips
----
- SQLite FTS5 syntax supported: phrases ("build plan"), prefix (mig*), boolean (plan AND users)
- Results are ordered by bm25 score (best matches first)
- Limit defaults to 20; raise for broad queries

Query examples
---------------
- Phrase search: `"build plan"`
- Prefix: `migrat*`
- Boolean: `plan AND users`
- Require urgent: `urgent AND deployment`

Parameters
----------
project_key : str
    Project identifier.
query : str
    FTS5 query string.
limit : int
    Max results to return.

Returns
-------
list[dict]
    Each entry: { id, subject, importance, ack_required, created_ts, thread_id, from }

Example
-------
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"10","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"search_messages","arguments":{
  "project_key":"/abs/path/backend","query":""build plan" AND users", "limit": 50
}}}
```

entries.name: mcp__mcp-agent-mail__send_message
entries.description:
Send a Markdown message to one or more recipients and persist canonical and mailbox copies to Git.

Discovery
---------
To discover available agent names for recipients, use: resource://agents/{project_key}
Agent names are NOT the same as program names or user names.

What this does
--------------
- Stores message (and recipients) in the database; updates sender's activity
- Writes a canonical `.md` under `messages/YYYY/MM/`
- Writes sender outbox and per-recipient inbox copies
- Optionally converts referenced images to WebP and embeds small images inline
- Supports explicit attachments via `attachment_paths` in addition to inline references

Parameters
----------
project_key : str
    Project identifier (same used with `ensure_project`/`register_agent`).
sender_name : str
    Must match an agent registered in the project.
to : list[str]
    Primary recipients (agent names). At least one of to/cc/bcc must be non-empty.
subject : str
    Short subject line that will be visible in inbox/outbox and search results.
body_md : str
    GitHub-Flavored Markdown body. Image references can be file paths or data URIs.
cc, bcc : Optional[list[str]]
    Additional recipients by name.
attachment_paths : Optional[list[str]]
    Extra file paths to include as attachments; will be converted to WebP and stored.
convert_images : Optional[bool]
    Overrides server default for image conversion/inlining. If None, server settings apply.
    Note: sender attachments_policy "inline"/"file" always forces conversion/inlining.
importance : str
    One of {"low","normal","high","urgent"} (free form tolerated; used by filters).
ack_required : bool
    If true, recipients should call `acknowledge_message` after reading.
thread_id : Optional[str]
    If provided, message will be associated with an existing thread.
broadcast : bool
    If true and `to` is empty, expand recipients to all registered agents in the
    project (excluding the sender). Mutually exclusive with explicit `to` recipients.
    Respects contact_policy settings — agents with block_all are skipped.
topic : Optional[str]
    Optional topic tag (alphanumeric + hyphens, max 64 chars). Stored on the message
    for topic-based filtering via fetch_inbox(topic=...) or fetch_topic().

Returns
-------
dict
    {
      "deliveries": [ { "project": str, "payload": { ... message payload ... } } ],
      "count": int
    }

Edge cases
----------
- If no recipients are given, the call fails.
- Unknown recipient names fail fast; register them first.
- Non-absolute attachment paths are resolved relative to the project archive root.

Do / Don't
----------
Do:
- Keep subjects concise and specific (aim for ≤ 80 characters).
- Use `thread_id` (or `reply_message`) to keep related discussion in a single thread.
- Address only relevant recipients; use CC/BCC sparingly and intentionally.
- Prefer Markdown links; attach images only when they materially aid understanding. The server
  auto-converts images to WebP and may inline small images depending on policy.

Don't:
- Send large, repeated binaries—reuse prior attachments via `attachment_paths` when possible.
- Change topics mid-thread—start a new thread for a new subject.
- Broadcast to "all" agents unnecessarily—target just the agents who need to act.

Examples
--------
1) Simple message:
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"5","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"send_message","arguments":{
  "project_key":"/abs/path/backend","sender_name":"GreenCastle","to":["BlueLake"],
  "subject":"Plan for /api/users","body_md":"See below."
}}}
```

2) Inline image (auto-convert to WebP and inline if small):
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"6a","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"send_message","arguments":{
  "project_key":"/abs/path/backend","sender_name":"GreenCastle","to":["BlueLake"],
  "subject":"Diagram","body_md":"![diagram](docs/flow.png)","convert_images":true
}}}
```

3) Explicit attachments:
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"6b","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"send_message","arguments":{
  "project_key":"/abs/path/backend","sender_name":"GreenCastle","to":["BlueLake"],
  "subject":"Screenshots","body_md":"Please review.","attachment_paths":["shots/a.png","shots/b.png"]
}}}
```

**Updated:** 2026-10-17 02:51 UTC

**Separate candidate branch:** `6151a231e9179c109cfbe8cff87e0a4148587b6a` (`v1/candidate-1`)
**Disposition:** `BLOCKED`; no RC exists and no qualification run has been accepted.

This checkpoint reconciles the candidate ledger and acceptance procedure against recorded source and test evidence. It is not a release approval. The historical `v1_release_readiness_report.md` cited in the task was not present in the inspected repository or worktrees; this file records evidence within the existing v1 documentation package.

## Current state update (2026-10-17)

- `v1/integration` is at `8c9994596144c5674d9be8e011ad1feb4109ffb4`; `v1/candidate-1` remains at `6151a231e9179c109cfbe8cff87e0a4148587b6a`. The integration branch is published to `origin/v1/integration` and has draft PR [#8](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/8) targeting `main`. The PR is not qualified or merge-ready.
- A confirmed CI dependency defect was fixed at `642ba37`: the contest-contract job now builds the CLI after installing dependencies and before running demo tests, because `cli/dist` is generated and untracked. The exact sequence passed locally with an isolated `HOME`; independent review accepted the workflow correction. CI run [38996098125](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions/runs/38996098125) on the current HEAD has passed `cloudflare-contest-contract`; Node 20/22/24 CLI matrix jobs are still running and the package job has not started. The earlier run [38995718946](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions/runs/38995718946) also has the contest job passed and its matrix still running at this checkpoint. The prior run at `10fe416` failed when `demo/lib/real-agent-runner.mjs` could not import `cli/dist/client.js`; that failure remains historical evidence.
- `rust-toolchain.toml` is tracked and pins Rust `1.95.0` with `rustfmt` and `clippy`; the suspected missing toolchain pin is not a defect.
- `REQ-DX-106` is satisfied on the integration branch: GitHub milestone [v1.0.0](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/milestone/1) has seven open plan-group issues ([#1–#7](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/issues/1)). The ledger checker reported 121 rows: 106 tested, 6 partial, 2 implemented and 7 open. This governance work does not qualify an RC or close a behavioral gate.

The other 20 fixture-arm tasks were found to use unsupported object-valued `setup` metadata and private validators depending on `validate_corpus.py`/in-process source execution, outside the accepted runner contract. No private checker was executed in that harness. Candidate v16 is being rewritten to use the actual runner schema and isolated validator subprocesses. The initial 20-case Docker batch yielded 0/20 valid outcomes because its process could not traverse host-owned private validator directories; that infrastructure failure remains preserved and is not task-behavior evidence. In a later Docker attempt, the author stopped after one PASS because the harness exposed `hidden/` while combining task source and private tests and did not establish the accepted candidate boundary; this is not accepted fixture validation, and the other 19 tasks remain unvalidated. The author has been instructed to stop using that Docker harness and use the repository's Bubblewrap validator boundary only, with candidate execution and private-oracle checks in separate processes. Neither v15 nor v16 is frozen, independently accepted, or qualification evidence; peer calibration, Node runtime parity, custody and sealing remain outstanding.
- The T4 denominator conflict (eight stated classes versus nine enumerated cases) and CJK/Hangul tokenizer acceptance conflict remain unresolved owner/spec decisions. T3 authoring, manual terminal acceptance, M5 execution, independent acceptance, exact-RC package checks, cross-runner reproducibility and publication remain pending.

This checkpoint intentionally stores no runtime credentials or test payloads.

It is preserved at `/tmp/nexus-v1-make-test-6151.log` (SHA-256 `7c4a364daedc3b26bd6b0392f6e0466c581c33ae5ef9d04c11348129e0abbb31`) and is superseded only for the source-suite result by the correctly ordered build-then-test run. name: Cross-Runner Reproducibility

      - name: Install cargo tools
        run: |

          export PATH="$CARGO_HOME/bin:$PATH"
          cargo install cargo-audit --locked --version 0.22.2

          mv "$RUNNER_TEMP/cargo-cyclonedx-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/cargo-cyclonedx" "$CARGO_HOME/bin/"
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-cli/releases/download/v0.33.1/cyclonedx-linux-x64 -o "$CARGO_HOME/bin/cyclonedx"

      - run: npm ci --prefix cli

Exit code 1
- **Hidden tests are out of the agent's reach.** `runAs` names a separate evaluator user. Candidate execution occurs
  inside the Bubblewrap mount namespace and does not bind the task store or validator sources; its `HOME`, `/tmp`,
  `/run`, and network namespace are isolated. Runtime files are explicit read-only binds. The harness grants the
  evaluator UID ACL access only to the disposable workspace, home and per-run proxy directory. Before qualification,
  verify the account and these existing operating-system permissions through the approved local setup procedure:
  1. `sudo useradd --system --create-home nexus-eval`
  2. A narrowly constrained sudoers rule permitting only the required Bubblewrap invocation as `nexus-eval`; do not

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# The sandbox requires --disable-userns. Ubuntu 22.04's bubblewrap 0.6.1 predates
# that option. Build a patched upstream release when the packaged executable
# lacks it; releases before 0.12.0 are affected by CVE-2026-87766.
readonly BWRAP=/usr/bin/bwrap
readonly SOURCE_URL=https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/releases/download/v0.13.1/bubblewrap-0.13.1.tar.xz
readonly SOURCE_SHA256=0e85c8702248b8dd64144f594147553650cdd0e4c951690345faace79c217c4d

supports_required_userns_control() {
  [[ -x "$BWRAP" ]] || return 1

  local version_output major minor patch
  version_output=$("$BWRAP" --version 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$version_output" =~ bubblewrap[[:space:]]+([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+) ]] || return 1
  major=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
  minor=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
  patch=${BASH_REMATCH[3]}
  ((major > 0 || minor > 12 || (minor == 12 && patch >= 0))) || return 1
  "$BWRAP" --help 2>&1 | grep -Fq -- '--disable-userns'
}

  "$BWRAP" --version
  exit 0
fi

systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect -p Delegate=yes -- /bin/sh -c '
S=/sys/fs/cgroup$(cut -d: -f3 /proc/self/cgroup); echo "scope=$S"; cat $S/cgroup.controllers
mkdir $S/sup $S/payload && echo $$ > $S/sup/cgroup.procs && echo "+cpu +memory +pids" > $S/cgroup.subtree_control && echo 67108864 > $S/payload/memory.max && echo 0 > $S/payload/memory.swap.max && echo 16 > $S/payload/pids.max && echo "50000 100000" > $S/payload/cpu.max && cat $S/payload/memory.max $S/payload/pids.max $S/payload/cpu.max
sh -c "echo \$\$ > $S/payload/cgroup.procs; exec python3 -c \"b=bytearray(200*1024*1024)\"" ; echo "hog rc=$?"; cat $S/payload/memory.events
sh -c "echo \$\$ > $S/payload/cgroup.procs; for i in \$(seq 40); do sleep 5 & done; wait" 2>&1 | tail -1; cat $S/payload/pids.events $S/payload/pids.peak
sh -c "echo \$\$ > $S/payload/cgroup.procs; setsid sh -c \"sleep 300\" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 & exit 0"; sleep 0.3; echo "survivors=$(wc -l < $S/payload/cgroup.procs)"; echo 1 > $S/payload/cgroup.kill; sleep 0.2; cat $S/payload/cgroup.events; cat $S/payload/memory.peak $S/payload/cpu.stat | head -3'

C=/home/mike/nexus-code/.git; TS=$(date -u +%FT%TZ); for f in FILE_.github_workflows_ci.yml FILE_.github_workflows_release.yml; do mkdir "$C/nexus-claims/$f" && printf '{"agent":"claude-code","branch":"v1/plan-10-pr-10i","since":"%s","pid":%s,"scope":"add ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh step after ensure-ci-bubblewrap.sh only (separate commit)"}\n' "$TS" $$ > "$C/nexus-claims/$f/owner.json" && echo "$TS CLAIM $f branch=v1/plan-10-pr-10i scope=one provisioning step after ensure-ci-bubblewrap.sh by=claude-code" >> "$C/nexus-claims.log" && echo claimed $f; done
cat > ~/nexus-wt/p10i/scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# The evaluator resource contract (eval/resources.mjs) runs each task-controlled
# command in a delegated transient systemd --user scope with the cpu, memory and
# pids cgroup v2 controllers. Hosted runners have no user manager for the runner
# account, and older systemd delegates only some controllers to user@.service.
# Provision both, then prove a delegated scope sees all three controllers.

uid="$(id -u)"
runtime="/run/user/$uid"

has_contract() {
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$runtime" DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=$runtime/bus" \
    systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect -p Delegate=yes -- \
    /bin/sh -c 'c=$(cat "/sys/fs/cgroup$(cut -d: -f3 /proc/self/cgroup)/cgroup.controllers"); for k in cpu memory pids; do case " $c " in *" $k "*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac; done' \
    2>/dev/null
}

if ! has_contract; then
  sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d
  printf '[Service]\nDelegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids\n' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/delegate.conf >/dev/null
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo loginctl enable-linger "$(id -un)"
  sudo systemctl restart "user@$uid.service"
  for _ in $(seq 50); do [[ -S "$runtime/bus" ]] && break; sleep 0.2; done
  has_contract || { echo "systemd user scopes with cpu, memory and pids delegation are unavailable" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

if [[ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ]]; then
  echo "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$runtime" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
  echo "DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=$runtime/bus" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
fi
echo "systemd user scope delegation: cpu memory pids"
EOF
chmod +x ~/nexus-wt/p10i/scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh && bash ~/nexus-wt/p10i/scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh

cat > ~/nexus-wt/p10i/scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# The evaluator resource contract (eval/resources.mjs) runs each task-controlled
# command in a delegated transient systemd --user scope with the cpu, memory and
# pids cgroup v2 controllers. Hosted runners have no user manager for the runner
# account, and older systemd delegates only some controllers to user@.service.
# Provision both, then prove a delegated scope sees all three controllers.

uid="$(id -u)"
runtime="/run/user/$uid"

has_contract() {
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$runtime" DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=$runtime/bus" \
    systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect -p Delegate=yes -- \
    /bin/sh -c 'c=$(cat "/sys/fs/cgroup$(cut -d: -f3 /proc/self/cgroup)/cgroup.controllers"); for k in cpu memory pids; do case " $c " in *" $k "*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac; done' \
    2>/dev/null
}

if ! has_contract; then
  sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d
  printf '[Service]\nDelegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids\n' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/delegate.conf >/dev/null
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo loginctl enable-linger "$(id -un)"
  sudo systemctl restart "user@$uid.service"
  for _ in $(seq 50); do [[ -S "$runtime/bus" ]] && break; sleep 0.2; done
  has_contract || { echo "systemd user scopes with cpu, memory and pids delegation are unavailable" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

if [[ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ]]; then
  echo "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$runtime" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
  echo "DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=$runtime/bus" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
fi
echo "systemd user scope delegation: cpu memory pids"
EOF
chmod +x ~/nexus-wt/p10i/scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh && bash ~/nexus-wt/p10i/scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh

  The limits are aggregate over the whole process tree, whatever its uid (`runAs`), session or process group.

  behaviour, using infrastructure fixtures only.

be tuned against held-out results.'''

## Summary

This PR is stacked on #18 (PR-10h), so review only the top two commits. It implements the kernel-enforced resource contract. Its absence kept qualification fail-closed: the README previously said the controls "do not currently establish kernel-enforced aggregate CPU, memory, process-count, or writable disk quotas".

Every task-controlled execution runs under `eval/cgroup_supervisor.mjs` inside its own delegated transient `systemd-run --user --scope`. That covers setup, the agent sandbox, legacy hidden and regression checks, every black-box oracle case, and the version probe.

- **Limits.** The supervisor writes cgroup v2 `cpu.max`, `memory.max`, `memory.swap.max=0` and `pids.max` on a `payload` leaf and reads them back. It refuses on any mismatch. The command joins the leaf before `exec`. The limits are aggregate over the process tree, across uid, session and process group.
- **Storage.** `resources.workspaceRoot` must be a tmpfs (checked with `statfs`). Workspace, home and sandbox `/tmp` pages are charged to the payload memcg and can't be swapped, so writable storage is kernel-bounded by `memoryBytes` per phase.
- **Cleanup.** Survivors are counted, then `cgroup.kill` runs, which reaches other uids and setsid daemons, and `populated 0` is proven. Timeouts kill through the cgroup, so the supervisor still reports.
- **Evidence.** Per-phase `resources` on each run record: limits, memoryPeak, oomKills, pidsPeak, pidsMaxEvents, cpu usage and throttle, survivors, cleaned. A missing report, failed read-back or uncleaned cgroup makes the run an error.
- **Preflight.** `qualificationResourceIsolationProblem(config)` requires `config.resources` and a contained probe on the host. Without them it still fails closed with the original message.
- **CI.** `scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh` provisions `Delegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids`, linger and a user manager on hosted runners. It is a separate workflow-only commit.

No thresholds, cases or held-out material were touched. Fixtures are infrastructure-only.

## Fixture evidence (local smoke, this host, kernel 6.8, systemd 255)

| Fixture | Limit | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| 300 MB memory hog | 128 MiB | exit 137, `oomKills 1`, cleaned |
| 40-way fork | `tasks 16` | `pidsMaxEvents 1`, `pidsPeak 16`, 15 survivors reaped |
| setsid daemon `sleep 300` | — | `survivorsAfterExit 1`, cleaned, no host survivor |
| 400 MB `dd` to tmpfs | 128 MiB | file 126 MiB, writer OOM-killed |

`cli/test/eval_integrity.test.ts` asserts these cases plus `/tmp` storage, CPU throttling at 20% and the timeout path, all through the real Bubblewrap path.

## Validation status

- Implemented and smoke-tested locally. The targeted test run is pending: the shared SUITE claim is held. CI on this PR is the exact-revision evidence.
- **Not yet qualification evidence.** Qualification still needs frozen limit values in the qualification config, the `nexus-eval` account (it does not exist on this host) and independent review.

Its absence kept qualification fail-closed: the README previously said the controls "do not currently establish kernel-enforced aggregate CPU, memory, process-count, or writable disk quotas".

Every task-controlled execution runs under `eval/cgroup_supervisor.mjs` inside its own delegated transient `systemd-run --user --scope`. That covers setup, the agent sandbox, legacy hidden and regression checks, every black-box oracle case, and the version probe.

- **Limits.** The supervisor writes cgroup v2 `cpu.max`, `memory.max`, `memory.swap.max=0` and `pids.max` on a `payload` leaf and reads them back. It refuses on any mismatch. The command joins the leaf before `exec`. The limits are aggregate over the process tree, across uid, session and process group.
- **Storage.** `resources.workspaceRoot` must be a tmpfs (checked with `statfs`). Workspace, home and sandbox `/tmp` pages are charged to the payload memcg and can't be swapped, so writable storage is kernel-bounded by `memoryBytes` per phase.
- **Cleanup.** Survivors are counted, then `cgroup.kill` runs, which reaches other uids and setsid daemons, and `populated 0` is proven. Timeouts kill through the cgroup, so the supervisor still reports.
- **Evidence.** Per-phase `resources` on each run record: limits, memoryPeak, oomKills, pidsPeak, pidsMaxEvents, cpu usage and throttle, survivors, cleaned. A missing report, failed read-back or uncleaned cgroup makes the run an error.
- **Preflight.** `qualificationResourceIsolationProblem(config)` requires `config.resources` and a contained probe on the host. Without them it still fails closed with the original message.
- **CI.** `scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh` provisions `Delegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids`, linger and a user manager on hosted runners. It is a separate workflow-only commit.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
VERSION=${1:?usage: package-linux.sh VERSION OUTPUT_DIR}
OUT=${2:?usage: package-linux.sh VERSION OUTPUT_DIR}
case "$VERSION" in v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;; *) echo "version must look like v1.2.3" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
mkdir -p "$OUT"
WORK=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

npm --prefix "$ROOT/cli" ci
npm --prefix "$ROOT/cli" run build
cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path "$ROOT/core/Cargo.toml" --bin harness-core --bin nexus-tui

PKG="$WORK/nexus"
mkdir -p "$PKG/bin" "$PKG/lib/core" "$PKG/lib/cli"
cp -R "$ROOT/cli/dist" "$PKG/lib/cli/dist"
cp "$ROOT/cli/package.json" "$ROOT/cli/package-lock.json" "$PKG/lib/cli/"
npm ci --omit=dev --prefix "$PKG/lib/cli"
cp "$ROOT/core/target/release/harness-core" "$ROOT/core/target/release/nexus-tui" "$PKG/lib/core/"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE" "$PKG/LICENSE"
printf '%s\n' "$VERSION" > "$PKG/VERSION"

cargo about generate -m "$ROOT/core/Cargo.toml" -c "$ROOT/about.toml" "$ROOT/about.hbs" > "$WORK/notices-rust.txt"
npx --yes license-checker-rseidelsohn --production --plainVertical --start "$PKG/lib/cli" > "$WORK/notices-npm.txt"
cat > "$PKG/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt" <<'EOF'
================================================================================
Nexus Code Third-Party Software Notices and Licenses
================================================================================

This package contains third-party software components licensed under open-source
licenses. The following sections provide notices and license texts for all
runtime and statically-linked dependencies included in this distribution.

================================================================================
Section 1: Rust Components (harness-core & nexus-tui)
================================================================================
EOF
cat "$WORK/notices-rust.txt" >> "$PKG/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt"
cat >> "$PKG/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt" <<'EOF'

================================================================================
Section 2: Node.js / npm Components (CLI Runtime)
================================================================================
EOF
cat "$WORK/notices-npm.txt" >> "$PKG/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt"
cp "$PKG/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt" "$OUT/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt"
cat > "$PKG/bin/nexus" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
NEXUS_HOME=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$(readlink -f -- "$0")")/.." && pwd)
export NEXUS_HOME
if [ -z "${NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS:-}" ] && [ -n "${HOME:-}" ] && [ -f "$HOME/.config/nexus/config.env" ]; then
  _ca=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "$HOME/.config/nexus/config.env" | tail -n 1 | sed "s/^['\"]//;s/['\"]$//")
  if [ -n "$_ca" ]; then
    case "$_ca" in
      "~/"*) _ca="$HOME/${_ca#\~/}" ;;
    esac
    export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="$_ca"

on:

    inputs:

        description: 'RC tag to package and compare (e.g. v1.0.0-rc.1)'
        required: true
        default: 'v1.0.0-rc.1'

        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        runner: [ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      COMMIT: ${{ inputs.commit }}
    steps:
      - name: Validate requested source identity
        run: |
          [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(-rc\\.[0-9]+)?$ ]] || { echo "version must be vX.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z-rc.N" >&2; exit 1; }

        with:

          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Require the tag, HEAD and a clean tree to be the requested commit
        run: |
          test "$(git rev-parse "refs/tags/$VERSION^{commit}")" = "$COMMIT" || { echo "tag $VERSION does not resolve to $COMMIT" >&2; exit 1; }
          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$COMMIT" || { echo "checked-out HEAD is not $COMMIT" >&2; exit 1; }
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)" || { echo "checkout is not clean" >&2; exit 1; }
          node scripts/sync-version.mjs --check --tag "$VERSION"
      - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install --yes make
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: cli/package-lock.json
''' + tools + '''      - run: npm ci --prefix cli
      - run: bash scripts/package-linux.sh "$VERSION" "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist"
      - name: Record source and toolchain identity
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/identity"
          node -e '
            const { createHash } = require("node:crypto");
            const { execSync } = require("node:child_process");
            const fs = require("node:fs");
            const sh = (c) => execSync(c, { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();
            const sha = (f) => createHash("sha256").update(fs.readFileSync(f)).digest("hex");
            const source = {
              version: process.env.VERSION,
              commit: sh("git rev-parse HEAD"),
              tree: sh("git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}"),
              tagObject: sh(`git rev-parse refs/tags/${process.env.VERSION}`),
              lockfiles: Object.fromEntries(["cli/package-lock.json", "core/Cargo.lock", "rust-toolchain.toml"].map((f) => [f, sha(f)])),
            };
            const toolchain = { node: process.version, npm: sh("npm --version"), rustc: sh("rustc -V"), cargo: sh("cargo -V") };
            const runner = { label: process.argv[1], image: process.env.ImageOS ?? null, imageVersion: process.env.ImageVersion ?? null };
            const dist = process.env.RUNNER_TEMP + "/dist";
            const artifacts = Object.fromEntries(fs.readdirSync(dist).sort().map((f) => [f, sha(dist + "/" + f)]));
            fs.writeFileSync(process.env.RUNNER_TEMP + "/identity/source-identity.json", JSON.stringify({ source, toolchain, runner, artifacts }, null, 2) + "\\n");
          ' "${{ matrix.runner }}"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/identity/source-identity.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:

          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: identity-${{ matrix.runner }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/identity/source-identity.json
          if-no-files-found: error

    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    env:

          diff <(ls "$A") <(ls "$B")
          node -e '
            const fs = require("node:fs");
            const [a, b] = ["ubuntu-22.04", "ubuntu-24.04"].map((r) => JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(`/tmp/repro/identity-${r}/source-identity.json`, "utf8")));
            const fail = (m) => { console.error(m); process.exit(1); };
            for (const id of [a, b]) {

          cat /tmp/repro/repro-evidence.json
          echo "CROSS_RUNNER_REPRO_PASS: $VERSION@$COMMIT byte-identical across ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-24.04."
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: repro-evidence
          path: /tmp/repro/repro-evidence.json
          if-no-files-found: error

I worked one likely reviewer question through myself: could a same-UID payload write its own PID into the `supervisor` leaf and escape its limits? Inside the sandbox it can't: Bubblewrap doesn't mount `/sys`, so cgroupfs isn't reachable at all. Under `runAs`, the cgroup files are also owned by the operator UID. I'll add that note to #19 after the review comes back.

Waiting on CI for #18–#20 and the independent review.

**Done so far**

- **Baseline:** `origin/v1/integration` is at `19dedc6` (after PR #14), so the `d2c4bfc` and `2c70d39` reports are both out of date. Open PRs before mine: #8, #9, #13, #15, #16, #17.
- **kiro-cli takeover:** on your confirmation, I closed its 20 claims and logged each one. I left its worktree untouched. Its last commit (`f1886a1`) has unresolved conflict markers committed into `eval/oracle.mjs`, so I didn't build on it.
- **PR #18 (PR-10h):** workspace history isolation. Before, repo-task workspaces kept a link to the full upstream clone, so a single `git log --all` showed the reference fix for every held-out task. Workspaces now contain only the pinned commit and its ancestors, and staging refuses to run if anything more is reachable. A negative test covers this.
- **PR #19 (PR-10i, stacked on #18):** kernel-enforced CPU, memory, process-count and storage limits for every task-controlled execution, with cleanup that catches escaped processes. Local fixtures behaved as intended: the memory hog was OOM-killed, the fork bomb was capped, the tmpfs filler stopped at the limit, and a daemonized process was found and killed. The new CI provisioning step passed on all three hosted runners.

Each runner records its source and toolchain identity, and the comparison requires those to match as well as the bytes. This answers codex-lead's request.

- None of #18–#20 is independently accepted or integrated yet.
- I haven't run the targeted tests locally. opencode has held the shared `SUITE` lock since 03:03Z, well past its declared 15 minutes, and hasn't posted since 03:15Z. PR CI is the exact-revision evidence for now.

I found no path from a descendant object, ref, packed ref, reflog, tag or cache path into the workspace. I did not run the new test.

Why the staging holds:
- A fresh `git init` plus `fetch <sha>` transfers only objects reachable from that commit through upload-pack, so no descendant object can be copied. It creates no alternates, remote, tags, `packed-refs` or `FETCH_HEAD`, and the reflog holds only the checkout.

- The cache is never mounted into the sandbox, and nothing records its path in `.git`.

1. `cli/test/eval_integrity.test.ts` (new test, "Control" block) — the control only asserts `/alternates/`. It never proves the child commit is reachable in the `--shared` layout. If `workspaceHistoryProblem` regressed to check only alternates, the control would still pass. Fix: also assert `git cat-file -e child` succeeds in `leaky` (and fails in `ws`, as it already does).
2. `eval/workspace.mjs:21` — `workspaceHistoryProblem` does not check `.git/config` for `url`/`insteadOf` entries or `info/grafts`. Neither can arise from the current staging, so this is defense-in-depth only.

## PR #19 (10i, resource contract): CHANGES REQUIRED

Every task-controlled spawn is routed through `spawnContained`:
- setup commands
- candidate agent
- black-box oracle
- legacy hidden and regression checks
- agent version probe

The remaining `spawnSync` calls in `run.mjs` and `workspace.mjs`, and the one in `isolate.mjs`, are trusted. I found no uncontained path. `node --check` passes on `resources.mjs` and `cgroup_supervisor.mjs`.

I also checked these and found them sound:
- **Escape from the cgroup:** the bwrap sandbox mounts no `/sys`, so the payload cannot write `cgroup.procs`, including in the same-uid dev case.
- **fd 3 leak:** a local experiment shows the report fd does not reach the payload.
- **Running before the limits apply:** the shell joins the payload cgroup before `exec`.

Blockers:
1. `eval/README.md`, "Resource contract" bullet 2 — the claim "the agent's writes stay charged after it exits" is false, and the storage bound is overstated. When a scope is removed, the kernel reparents tmpfs charges to the parent cgroup, where nothing limits them.
   - **Failure scenario:** the agent fills about `memoryBytes` of tmpfs and exits. The hidden and regression phases each get a fresh `memory.max` and can write another `memoryBytes`. Total retained storage is about 3x `memoryBytes` or more, bounded only by the tmpfs default of 50% of RAM.
   - **Fix:** mount the `workspaceRoot` tmpfs with an explicit `size=` and have preflight verify it (`statfs` blocks, not only the magic number). Then reword the README: "per-phase charge, plus a hard tmpfs size cap".
2. `eval/resources.mjs`, `kill()` (about line 66) — a kill that arrives before the shell has joined the payload leaf is lost. `cgroup.kill` on an empty leaf succeeds and returns, and the payload then starts unkilled. The report arrives before `spawn`, so overflow or timeout handling could hit this window.
   - **Failure scenario:** `kill()` is called right after the cgroup path is reported. The cgroup kill hits an empty leaf and the 10s fallback is cleared. The payload runs to natural exit, and `close` never fires until then.
   - **Fix:** have the supervisor emit a second `{joined:true}` line after the shell joins the payload cgroup. Until then, `kill()` should also SIGTERM the supervisor, and the supervisor should check a "stop requested" flag before spawning. Or make `kill()` retry the cgroup write until `populated 0`.

Non-blocking:
3. `eval/cgroup_supervisor.mjs`, `finish` — SIGKILL or OOM of the supervisor leaves the payload orphaned until the harness `close` handler runs `cgroup.kill`. Fail-closed holds, since there is no report, but nothing restricts the payload in the meantime. The fallback `process.kill(-pid)` misses setsid'd processes. Fix: the harness fallback should always write `cgroup.kill` as well.
4. `eval/cgroup_supervisor.mjs:~35` — `memory.max` read-back differs when `memoryBytes` is not a multiple of the page size. Fix: validate `memoryBytes % 4096 === 0` in `resourceConfigProblem`.
5. `memory.oom.group` is not set. An OOM kill of a validator child can make a check fail rather than error. Fix: set `memory.oom.group=1` and treat `oomKills>0` in hidden or regression phases as a containment error.
6. `cli/test/eval_integrity.test.ts` — the new test asserts `qualificationResourceIsolationProblem({resources: ok}) === null`, so it hard-fails on any host without a user systemd manager. Fix: gate it on an env flag, as the CI step does.
7. `scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh` delegates `cpuset io`, which is not needed. Fix: use `Delegate=cpu memory pids`.

No acceptance thresholds are weakened. Qualification moves from always-blocked to blocked unless the probe passes. The 64 MiB, 8 task and 10% floors are minimums only.

## PR #20 (7e, repro identity): ACCEPT WITH NITS

Script injection: none. `version` and `commit` are validated by regex in a step before checkout, they reach shell only through `env:`, and `${{ inputs.version }}` in `with:` is not shell-evaluated. `actionlint` is clean and `node --check` passes. I could not run the unit test because `~/nexus-wt/p07e` has no `node_modules`.

The wrong-ref risk is covered: tag→commit, `HEAD==commit`, a clean tree, `sync-version --tag` and a full-SHA requirement. Evidence records `commit`, `tree` and `tagObject`. The `compare` job also fails on any commit mismatch.

Findings:
1. `.github/workflows/repro.yml` ("Record source and toolchain identity") — there is no clean-tree and HEAD re-check after `package-linux.sh`. The identity records `HEAD^{tree}`, not the working tree. If `npm ci` or the packaging scripts dirty tracked files, the artifacts no longer match the recorded commit, and both runners could do this identically. Fix: run `git status --porcelain` and `git rev-parse HEAD` again inside `record` (or just before it), and fail on any difference.
2. `scripts/repro-identity.mjs`, `compare` — builder distinctness is by `runner.label`, which comes from the workflow matrix. `image` and `imageVersion` may be null and are not required or compared. Fix: require non-null `ImageOS` and `ImageVersion`, and require the builder labels to equal the expected set `{ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04}`.
3. The evidence does not bind the workflow itself. `workflow_dispatch` runs the workflow file from whatever ref was dispatched, and the evidence records neither `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA` nor `GITHUB_REF`. A modified `repro.yml` on a branch could produce a PASS. Fix: record `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA`, `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` and `GITHUB_REF` in the evidence, and require the workflow ref to be protected.
4. Nit: the tools downloaded by `curl` (cargo-deny, cargo-about, cyclonedx) have no checksum verification, and the actions are pinned by tag, not SHA. This is pre-existing, but it matters for release provenance.</result>

If `npm ci` or the packaging scripts dirty tracked files, the artifacts no longer match the recorded commit, and both runners could do this identically. Fix: run `git status --porcelain` and `git rev-parse HEAD` again inside `record` (or just before it), and fail on any difference.
2. `scripts/repro-identity.mjs`, `compare` — builder distinctness is by `runner.label`, which comes from the workflow matrix. `image` and `imageVersion` may be null and are not required or compared. Fix: require non-null `ImageOS` and `ImageVersion`, and require the builder labels to equal the expected set `{ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04}`.
3. The evidence does not bind the workflow itself. `workflow_dispatch` runs the workflow file from whatever ref was dispatched, and the evidence records neither `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA` nor `GITHUB_REF`. A modified `repro.yml` on a branch could produce a PASS. Fix: record `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA`, `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` and `GITHUB_REF` in the evidence, and require the workflow ref to be protected.
4. Nit: the tools downloaded by `curl` (cargo-deny, cargo-about, cyclonedx) have no checksum verification, and the actions are pinned by tag, not SHA. This is pre-existing, but it matters for release provenance.</result>

content.text:
The reviewer's findings hold up, and two are real blockers on #19. Here's what I'll change:

**#19 blockers**
- **Storage:** I overstated the bound. When a phase's cgroup is removed, the kernel moves its tmpfs charges to the unlimited parent, so phases add up. Fix: a required `storageBytes`, and `workspaceRoot` must be a tmpfs whose total size is at most that. That cap is enforced by the filesystem itself.
- **Kill race:** a kill can land before the payload joins its cgroup. Fix: once a kill is requested, the harness keeps writing `cgroup.kill` until the supervisor exits.

**#19, also taking**
- The harness always writes `cgroup.kill` as its fallback.
- `memoryBytes` must be page-aligned.
- `memory.oom.group=1`.
- Delegate only `cpu memory pids`.

**#19, declining with reasons**
- I won't treat an OOM during hidden tests as an error. That would let candidate code make its own runs unscored; it stays a fail.
- I won't gate the host-proof test. The repo's zero-skip rule requires the real host feature, as it already does for Bubblewrap.

**#20**
- Re-check HEAD and a clean tree after the build.
- Require runner image identity and the exact builder set.
- Bind the workflow to `refs/tags/<version>` and record the workflow SHA, ref and attempt.
- Unpinned tool downloads are a pre-existing gap; I'll note it, not fix it here.

**#18**
- Strengthen the control so it proves the child commit is actually reachable in the leaky layout.

cd ~/nexus-wt/p10i && git add -A eval cli/test/eval_integrity.test.ts scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh && git commit -q -m "security(eval): cap run storage with a dedicated tmpfs and close the early-kill race

Independent review of PR #19:
- tmpfs charges reparent to the unlimited parent when a phase's cgroup is
  removed, so per-phase memory.max did not bound storage across phases.
  Require resources.storageBytes and a workspaceRoot tmpfs no larger than
  it (statfs size), refuse --keep, and correct the README claim.
- a kill requested before the payload joined its leaf was lost. The
  harness now keeps emptying the payload leaf until the supervisor exits,
  SIGTERMs the supervisor (which also repeats the kill), and kills it after
  10 s; the close handler always empties the leaf as a fallback.
- set memory.oom.group=1 so an OOM ends the whole phase; require
  page-aligned memoryBytes so the read-back matches.
- delegate only cpu memory pids in CI.
OOM in hidden/regression stays a candidate outcome (failed check), not an
infrastructure error, so candidate code cannot make its own runs unscored.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

Run `git -C /home/mike/nexus-code fetch -q origin` first. New heads (rebased onto integration f8e19e4; integration is now f68b5bc, with only docs/manifest merges since):
- #18 origin/v1/plan-10-pr-10h = 0a75ef2. Fix commit 0a75ef2: the control now asserts the child is reachable in the --shared layout, plus a second control — a full --no-local clone with the remote removed — that must be detected by non-ancestor reachability (not alternates). CI green on 0a75ef2 (run 39095342308).
- #19 origin/v1/plan-10-pr-10i = b12edc0. Fix commits 21e2055 and b12edc0 (diff: `git diff 86b9062 b12edc0`).
  - B1: required resources.storageBytes; workspaceRoot must be a tmpfs with statfs size <= storageBytes; --keep refused; README reworded (reparenting acknowledged; the tmpfs size is the cross-phase cap).
  - B2: kill() now writes cgroup.kill, SIGTERMs the supervisor, repeats cgroup.kill every 50 ms until child close, and SIGKILLs the supervisor group after 10 s. The supervisor's stop() also repeats cgroup.kill, and the close handler always empties the leaf.
  - Also: page-aligned memoryBytes, memory.oom.group=1, Delegate=cpu memory pids, and a test for the immediate-kill case.
  - Declined: OOM in hidden/regression stays a failed check, not a containment error, so a candidate cannot make its own runs unscored. Also declined: env-gating the host-proof test, because the repo's zero-skip rule mirrors the existing real-Bubblewrap requirement.
  - CI at the prior head 7366235 failed exactly one test (black-box oracle exact-shape deepEqual, caused by the new resources key), now fixed in b12edc0. CI for b12edc0 is running (run 39102595299).
- #20 origin/v1/plan-07-pr-7e-repro-identity = 8da5a1f. Fix commit 8da5a1f:
  - record fails if packaging dirtied tracked files.
  - compare requires exactly {ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04}, non-null image and imageVersion, one run id/attempt, and workflow ref == refs/tags/<version> with workflow sha == commit.
  - The workflow validate step requires GITHUB_REF == refs/tags/$VERSION and GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA == $COMMIT.
  - Tool checksum pinning is noted as pre-existing and out of scope.
  - repro_identity.test.ts passes locally 1/1; CI green on 8da5a1f (run 39095319456).

Return per PR: ACCEPT / ACCEPT WITH NITS / CHANGES REQUIRED, with any remaining findings (file:line plus failure scenario). Also state whether you accept or contest the two declined items. Under 450 words.

- **Storage limit (#19):** I had overstated it. When one phase of a run finishes, the kernel stops counting its disk use against any limit, so phases added up. The cross-phase limit now comes from a dedicated, size-capped tmpfs (`storageBytes`). I corrected the README and refuse `--keep`.
- **Early stop (#19):** a stop requested before the task joined its limit group could be lost. The harness now repeats the kill until the supervisor exits.
- **#20:** the run fails if packaging modified tracked files. It also requires both named Ubuntu runners with recorded images, and requires the workflow to run from the RC tag itself, so an edited copy on a branch can't produce a pass.
- **#18:** the test now proves its control cases really expose the fix commit, so detection doesn't rest on one signal.

I declined two suggestions, and the reviewer can contest either:
- **Out-of-memory during hidden tests** stays a failed check, not an infrastructure error. Otherwise candidate code could make its own runs unscored.
- **The host-feature test** isn't skipped on machines without systemd. That matches the repo's no-skip rule for Bubblewrap.

**Coordination**

- I released the shared test lock (SUITE). My local rerun stalled during the usage-limit pause, and I'm not counting it as a result; CI is the evidence.
- Integration is now at `f68b5bc`. The merges since my rebase touched only the held-out manifest, the custody report and two ledger rows, none of my files.

**Next:** once each PR is accepted and green, I'll rebase onto the latest integration head and merge #18, then #19, then #20. Then I'll release my claims and take the exact-RC packaging and version-validation lane.

**Still needed from you before qualification can run on #19**
- Choose and freeze the `resources` values in the qualification config.
- Mount a dedicated size-capped tmpfs for evaluation workspaces.
- Create the `nexus-eval` account.

<result>## PR #18 (10h): ACCEPT

Both of my earlier nits are fixed in 0a75ef2.
- The `--shared` control now asserts the child commit is actually reachable.
- The new `--no-local` clone with the remote removed has no alternates, and it is still detected by the "not ancestors" reachability check. That proves the detection does not depend on alternates.

I found nothing remaining. I did not run the test locally.

## PR #19 (10i): ACCEPT WITH NITS

- **B1 (storage cap):** fixed. `storageBytes` is required and `statfs` size must be at most `storageBytes`. `--keep` is refused, and the README now says the filesystem cap is the cross-phase bound and acknowledges the reparenting.
- **B2 (lost kill):**
  - The harness `kill()` now writes `cgroup.kill`, SIGTERMs the supervisor, and repeats the write every 50 ms until `close`. It SIGKILLs the supervisor group after 10 s.
  - The supervisor's `stop()` also repeats the write, and the `close` handler always empties the leaf. This closes the window where a kill reached an empty leaf before the payload joined.
  - The new early-kill test covers that window.
- **Other fixes:** page alignment, `memory.oom.group=1` (now read back) and `Delegate=cpu memory pids` all check out.

Remaining nits, none blocking:
1. `eval/resources.mjs` (`resourceConfigProblem`) — the tmpfs size check is declarative.
   - **Failure scenario:** `/dev/shm` passes if `storageBytes` is set to its full size, which is half of RAM. The cap is then "half of RAM", and other tenants share it.
   - **Fix:** the qualification config should pin the mount path and size, and the README should say shared tmpfs only counts as a cap when `storageBytes` equals its size. The README already half-says this.
2. `eval/resources.mjs` (`kill()`) — the 50 ms interval is not unref'd. If `child.close` never fires, for example because the supervisor is gone and an escaped process holds a stdio pipe, the harness keeps writing `cgroup.kill` indefinitely. The 10 s group SIGKILL does not stop the interval. In practice repeated `cgroup.kill` empties the leaf, which closes the pipes and fires `close`, so this is low risk. **Fix:** cap the repeat at about 30 s.
3. `memory.oom.group=1` combined with an OOM in a hidden or regression check scoring as a failed check is acceptable. See item 1 below.

**Declined items:**
1. **OOM in hidden/regression scored as a failed check: I accept.**
   - After reparenting, a validator's cgroup carries none of the candidate's charges. An OOM there is the validator hitting its own frozen `memoryBytes` limit.
   - Counting it as an infrastructure error would let a candidate make its own runs unscored by consuming memory. A failed check is the fail-closed outcome.
   - The caveat is that the frozen limits must be calibrated so the reference solution passes with headroom. That is a corpus-calibration task, not a code change.
2. **No env-gating for the host-proof test: I accept.** A hard failure on hosts without systemd delegation matches the existing real-Bubblewrap rule. The provisioning script covers CI.

## PR #20 (7e): ACCEPT

All three findings are fixed:
- `record` now fails if packaging dirtied tracked files, using `status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`.
- `compare` requires exactly the two expected builder labels and non-null image and imageVersion. It also requires the workflow ref to be `refs/tags/<version>` with the workflow sha equal to the commit, and a single run id and attempt.
- The validate step enforces `GITHUB_REF` and `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA` before checkout, so a branch-modified workflow cannot produce evidence.

One nit: the dirty check ignores untracked files, deliberately, because build outputs exist. An untracked source file added by packaging would be bundled without being recorded. That is low risk given the tree and artifact digest comparison. **Fix:** also record `git status --porcelain --ignored=no` output into the evidence if you want it airtight.</result>

p='eval/resources.mjs'; s=open(p).read()
old='''    repeat = setInterval(killPayload, 50);

content.content:
## 1.1 Release-candidate lifecycle and evidence identity

The release sequence has five distinct stages. Passing an earlier stage is a prerequisite for the next stage, not a substitute for it. Every G0–G4 acceptance ID remains mandatory; the stage determines which exact input and evidence it evaluates, not whether the check applies.

1. **Pre-RC source gates.** Before creating an RC tag, run required source CI and every G0–G4 check whose acceptance method evaluates source, a source-built test binary, or an environment without requiring a published RC. Record the full commit ID and check results. Source checks do not establish behavior of the installed package.
2. **RC artifact construction.** After the required owner authorization, create the version-matched RC tag on that exact source commit and use the repository release workflow to build and publish the RC artifacts. Record the workflow run, tag commit, artifact digests, and provenance. The workflow-produced artifacts are the candidates for qualification; a local build or a different commit is not interchangeable. RC artifact publication is not product qualification or final release acceptance.
3. **RC artifact gates.** Before installed-RC product qualification, run every G0–G4 check whose acceptance method requires the RC archive, RC attestation/release, or workflow-produced artifact. This includes ACC-SUP-01/02/03/06/08. ACC-PKG checks that explicitly require an installed package run against this RC as specified by their test method. Record the RC tag commit, workflow run, artifact digests, and each check result. A source-level analogue does not replace an artifact-bound check.
4. **Installed-RC qualification.** Install the workflow-produced RC package using the documented procedure and run the applicable product, provider, task-quality, terminal, installation, and independent-acceptance gates in §§4–8. Bind each result to both the RC source commit and installed package digest. If a source change or rebuilt artifact changes either identity, rerun every affected gate against the new candidate and retain prior results as historical evidence.
5. **Stable promotion and publication.** After exact-RC acceptance and G6 pass, create a stable-version commit directly on the accepted RC commit, changing only the synchronized version metadata required for v1.0.0. Record both commits and the version-only diff. Run required source CI and all applicable source G0–G4 checks on this exact stable-version commit before tagging. If any other source changes, restart RC construction and qualification. Then create the `v1.0.0` tag on that checked commit and build a draft release. Keep its assets unpublished while verifying the stable artifact identity, provenance, package contents, installation, and publication metadata. Compare the stable package contents with the accepted RC; if packaged behavior or content differs beyond version-specific metadata, rerun affected installed-RC qualification gates and obtain independent acceptance for the stable artifact. Publish the draft only after these checks pass and the signed acceptance disposition is recorded. Record the published digests and provenance.

The final G6 decision in §10 applies to promoting the accepted RC toward a stable release. It requires the applicable gates to pass for the accepted RC and authorizes the version-only stable commit and its source checks, followed by the stable tag and draft build; it does not waive source CI, artifact identity, installed-RC qualification, or any threshold. Public publication is a separate post-build gate in stage 5 above. The release workflow must keep stable assets in draft state until stable artifact checks pass. The current tag-triggered workflow publishes immediately and therefore cannot be used for stable publication until it supports this draft-then-publish sequence.

## 1. Rules

1. The RC is built and published by the release workflow from a clean tag. Its version is identical across all components (REQ-REL-103).
2. All qualification runs use the **installed RC package**, installed with the documented one-line command. They never use a checkout build. The only exception is CI unit and PTY suites, which run from source at the same commit.
3. Thresholds (DEC-05) are frozen before the first M5 run. A failing gate is fixed in code and the run is repeated as `rc.N+1`. A threshold is never relaxed after results are known.
4. Evidence goes to `docs/reviews/evidence/v1-qualification/<rc>/`. The directory contains:
   - `manifest.json`: commit, package sha256, environment, model fingerprint, dates;
   - raw outputs;
   - a `SHA256SUMS` file.

   Secrets are redacted before commit.
5. Any step that cannot run in the available environment is recorded as **NOT RUN** with its reason. A NOT RUN on a blocker gate fails the gate.

## 2. Environments

| ID | Environment | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | GitHub Actions: ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-24.04; Node 20, 22 and 24; pinned Rust | Unit, integration and PTY suites; packaging; reproducibility |
| E2 | Docker clean images: ubuntu:22.04, ubuntu:24.04, debian:12, fedora:40. Each with no Node, then with Node 20 and Node 22. Non-root user. | Installer, upgrade, rollback, uninstall, platform failure messages |
| E3 | Operator dev box: Linux x86-64, real terminals (xterm, kitty, tmux, VS Code terminal, GNOME Terminal) | Terminal matrix, live sessions |
| E4 | Homelab-ai gateway, the **only** inference path (DEC-16): direct, and through `eval/standalone/plain_proxy.mjs` | Task-quality runs, standalone qualification, T3/T4 |
| E5 | Cloud, small spend: ChatGPT sign-in (experimental tier) and OpenRouter with a pinned model; OpenAI and Anthropic keys if added | Provider verify; one live task per supported cloud provider |

## 3. Gate checklist (G0–G4: automated acceptance IDs)
## 10. Release decision (G6)

G6 passes only when every item below holds. It authorizes a version-only stable commit from the accepted RC source, followed by its source checks, stable tag, and unpublished draft candidate; it does not authorize making stable assets publicly available. RC tags are candidate construction inputs governed by §1.1; an RC tag or its successful build does not satisfy this release decision.

- [ ] G0–G4 automated gates pass on the final RC commit (§3).
- [ ] RC artifact gates pass on the workflow-produced RC, including ACC-SUP-01/02/03/06/08; record the exact source commit, workflow run, and artifact digest.
- [ ] §4 standalone and provider matrix: all rows PASS.
- [ ] §5 terminal acceptance: CI, scripted and manual gates PASS.
- [ ] §6 thresholds: all hold.
- [ ] §7 install matrix: all rows PASS.
- [ ] §8 independent acceptance: ACCEPT, or ACCEPT WITH DEFECTS with owner dispositions and no blocker defects outstanding.
- [ ] `scripts/check_requirements.mjs --enforce` passes:
  - every B row is `product-qualified`, or `tested` with a recorded justification for why product qualification does not apply;
  - every RR row is ≥ `tested`.
- [ ] Docs checklist (SPEC-09 §3.2) is signed off.
- [ ] Release notes state the standalone scope (DEC-16), the provider tiers (DEC-06), the experimental surfaces (DEC-03, DEC-07) and the known limitations.
- [ ] Owner approval to publish (X7).

After G6, complete source checks on the exact stable-version commit before tagging, then complete the stable artifact checks in §1.1 stage 5 before publishing the draft. A failure keeps publication blocked and requires remediation plus the applicable requalification; do not mark the campaign released until published artifacts are independently verified.

**Outcome recording.** The release decision record goes in `docs/releases/v1.0.0.md`, with links to every evidence directory.
