entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

lastPrompt: continue working collaboratively with the other active agents on getting to release completion.

content.text:
No one else's work is waiting on me right now, so I've stepped into an independent-reviewer role and set up a watch on the coordination log.

**What changed this round**
- **Retracted two of my own claims.** PR #33 (the hardened evaluator checks, now owned by eval-impl) already contains all three fixes from my handed-off branch. My branch is superseded and can be deleted once eval-impl acknowledges. I had also blamed the 13:11 host re-provision on an unidentified agent. The system journal shows it was run from PR #33's own worktree, so its different sudoers file and resource-profile digest are part of that branch's design. I corrected both statements on PR #33, on the readiness PR (#46), and in the log.
- **Volunteered as independent reviewer.** I offered the log read-only reviews of work I didn't write: antigravity's upgrade-recovery fixes, codex-api-root's compatibility PR (#47), readiness PRs, and the RC build checks. I said explicitly that I'm not independent for PR #33 or the host scripts, because I wrote parts of them.

**Where the release stands** (integration is at 6a16cb6; nothing tagged or published)
- **Critical path.** PR #33 has to merge before any held-out tests can run. Two reviewers asked for changes there, and eval-impl is working on them. Its latest host validation passed every check I could read.
- **In progress by others:**
  - antigravity: upgrade rollback and reinstall safety (PLAN-12).
  - codex-api-root: mixed-component version check (#47) and the readiness refresh (#46).
  - codex-lead: reconciling how an old blocker item (CTX-001) is classified.
- **Still failing the requirements check: 11 items.** Most can only be closed on an actual release candidate: the held-out evaluation, long-task runs, standalone and provider checks, the cross-machine reproducibility build, and the release security scan.

**Only you can do these**
- Run the real-terminal test matrix (5 environments × 3 window sizes) on the installed RC once it exists. The rules say automated tests can't stand in for it.
- Apply the branch-protection rulesets proposed in PR #23; that needs admin access.

The watch picks up log entries that mention me, review requests, merges, and RC or tag events. When one arrives I'll do the review or check it asks for.

content.text:
I've finished reviewing the 7 open GitHub issues. All of them are v1.0.0 tracking issues opened on 2026-10-17, none has been updated since, and several now lag well behind the work. I checked each one against `v1/integration` at 6a16cb6 and the claim log. I haven't posted anything on GitHub.

| # | Issue | Real state now | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#4** | Tokenizer floor vs the 1.5× band (REQ-AGT-118) | **Resolved.** The conflict is settled by DEC-17 (merged in PRs #11, #12, #14 and #15). REQ-AGT-118 is now `tested`; the Chinese 2.00× and Hangul 1.67× exceptions are kept, and `tokens.test.ts` passes. | **Close**, linking DEC-17 and the PR-11d review evidence. |
| **#1** | Finish and seal the held-out T2/T3 tasks | **Mostly done.** The 40 T2 tasks are sealed (merged in #16; manifest digest `50895b84…`, 10 per class and per language, all from external repos). The 8 T3 tasks are sealed. The custodian accepted both, and the stores are root-only. Its latest comment (the "v15" package was invalid) describes a version that's since been replaced. | **Keep open, but update it.** Two items are missing: (a) the custody reports never mention licenses (0 hits); the manifest only lists the `repo`; (b) the sealed tasks still use the old hidden-test format, and running them depends on PR #33 adding support for that format. Close once both are fixed. |
| **#2** | M5 qualification runs | **Not started; needs an RC.** Its comment says T4 counts 8 vs 9 fault classes. ACCEPTANCE §6.2 now says 9 × 5 (fixed in #13). **But `PLAN-10` task 11, line 34, still says "T4 (8×5)"**, so the plan still contradicts the acceptance doc. | Keep open. Post that §6.2 is settled, and fix the stale line in PLAN-10. Also note that PR #33 must merge before any held-out run. |
| **#5** | Cross-runner reproducibility on the RC | The workflow is merged (#20); it has never run on an RC. | Keep open. Post a link to `repro.yml` and note that it's waiting for the RC tag. |
| **#6** | Independent continuity and truncation acceptance | Not started; needs an RC and a reviewer who didn't build it. | Keep open. A reviewer needs to be picked. Every agent that worked on the continuity changes is ruled out, and I'm one of them. |
| **#3** | Real-terminal acceptance matrix | Not started. The procedure is merged (#24), but it needs the installed RC and **you** at real terminals (5 environments × 3 sizes). | Keep open; this one is yours. |
| **#7** | Final ledger and release gate | Not started; it closes last. The requirements check still fails on 11 rows at 6a16cb6. | Keep open. |

**Gaps across the issue list**
- **PR #33 has no issue,** although it's the current critical-path blocker for every held-out run. Several other items have no issue either: provisioning and validating the qualification host, the format mismatch, standalone/provider testing (REQ-PRV-003 and -111, each tracked only inside #2), and the release security scan (REQ-REL-005).
- **None of the issues say how far along they are.** Current status lives only in READINESS.md and the claim log, so GitHub alone doesn't show what blocks the release.

I can do the cleanup if you want: close #4, post a status comment on #1, #2 and #5, and open an issue for PR #33 and the host work. I'd send the one-line PLAN-10 fix to whoever owns that plan doc, since I don't hold a claim on it.

Track the current critical-path blocker for every held-out run (#1, #2). Until now it was tracked only in READINESS.md and the claim log.

## Current state (\`v1/integration\` @ \`6a16cb6\`, 2026-10-18)
- PR #33 (owner: eval-impl) is open at \`3db2cf4\`. Independent reviewers returned CHANGES-REQUIRED: a Python leak via candidate import of \`sitecustomize\`; Go/Rust compile-time embedding; and host-source mounts in \`agentSandboxArgv\` that \`runtimeCorpusOverlapProblem\` does not cover (comments 6252102243, 6252621855).
- The sealed heldout-v2 tasks use the legacy \`hidden\` format; PR #33 provides the hardened-legacy evaluator they need.
- Qualification host mike-dev: provisioned from PR #33's \`eval/host/provision.sh\` (13:11:29Z, sudoers \`99-nexus-eval\`, profile sha256 \`4e8d42a2…\`), with validation evidence \`validate-20261018T1311Z.json\` on that branch. Integration still lacks PR #33's runAs fixes, including the version-probe timeout drop at \`eval/run.mjs:355\`.

## Acceptance
- PR #33 rebased on current integration, findings fixed, exact-head CI green, independent re-review ACCEPT by a reviewer who implemented no part of it.
- Host validation re-run against the integrated scripts, bound to the integrated commit and the frozen profile digest.
- Thresholds are not weakened; failed runs are preserved as evidence.

References: PLAN-10 PR-10m; ACCEPTANCE.md §6.1; issues #1, #2.")

content.text:
The issue cleanup is done, and GitHub's tracking issues now match the actual release state.

- **#4 closed.** The tokenizer conflict was settled by DEC-17 (PRs #11, #12, #14 and #15), and REQ-AGT-118 is now `tested`. The closing comment says real-world qualification on the release candidate is still tracked in #2.
- **#1 updated.** The 40 T2 tasks and 8 T3 tasks are sealed, and the custodian accepted both. Two things still keep it open:
  - The custody reports contain no license records for the source repos. The custodian has to add these.
  - The sealed tasks use the old hidden-test format, and only PR #33 can run that format.
- **#2 updated.** The 8-vs-9 fault-class question is settled at 9 × 5 in the acceptance doc. No qualification run has started; they wait on a release candidate and PR #33.
- **#5 updated.** The two-runner reproducibility check exists (PR #20) but hasn't run yet, because no release candidate has been tagged. Running it falls to codex-api-root as release publisher.
- **#49 opened.** It tracks PR #33 and the qualification host, which together block every held-out run but had no issue. It lists the open review findings, the host provisioning and validation state, and what acceptance requires.
- **Plan doc fix requested.** `PLAN-10` line 34 still says "T4 (8×5)" while the acceptance doc says 9 × 5. I logged a request to whoever owns the plan doc instead of editing it, since I hold no claim on that file.

#3, #6 and #7 were accurate, so I left them unchanged. #3 is the real-terminal test matrix, which needs you at physical terminals once a release candidate exists. The log watch is still running and will alert me to review requests, merges, or release-candidate events.

v1/integration
Interrupted same-version upgrades could erase the only working package, and recovery could finalize a version shim without validating the runtime. This follow-up to rejected PR #48 journals rollback package identities outside disposable staging, restores the actual previous package across exception/crash boundaries, and reports manual intervention without discarding artifacts when restoration fails.

It also adds bounded exact runtime probes with process-group cleanup, complete private state/config backup restoration, read-only check purity, invalid-recovery exit status, packaged startup recovery, and bounded published-alpha compatibility. TUI gains a side-effect-free version response so new packages can verify all component versions. Embedded compatibility metadata is bound to the selected release even without a detached asset.

Validation at code commit b590be268b37790bfe4568694a9378f2016749b0: TypeScript no-emit build passed; 107/107 focused upgrade/compatibility tests passed on an isolated local WSL snapshot, including actual SIGKILL after package replacement, live wrong-version rollback, and descendant cleanup for hung probes. Official alpha.2 archive SHA-256 was verified and its historical runtime passed the new bounded helper on WSL. No mike-dev SUITE overlap, inference, or private held-out access occurred.

content.text: Confirmed: the installer accepts any `NEXUS_PREFIX`, so a root-owned shared install like `/usr/local` is reachable. I'm posting the review on PR #51.

input.command:
cd /home/mike/nexus-code; gh pr comment 51 --body "**Independent Review (\`claude-code\`, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)): CHANGES REQUESTED on \`b590be2\`**

Reviewer independence: I wrote no part of PLAN-12 or PR #48/#51. Read-only source review plus one local reproduction against \`tsc\` output of \`b590be2\`, in a scratch prefix. No SUITE claim, no inference, no held-out access.

### Blocking
**B1. Startup recovery bricks every launch of a non-writable install once any upgrade has completed.** \`performUpgrade\` leaves \`.upgrade-journal.json\` in place with \`state: \"complete\"\`. The new \`index.ts\` block calls \`recoverUpgrade(prefix)\` whenever that file exists. \`recoverUpgrade\` creates \`lib/nexus/.upgrade.lock\` (\`openSync(lock, \"wx\")\`) **before** \`recoverUpgradeLocked\` sees that the state needs no action. With an unwritable \`lib/nexus\` (e.g. \`NEXUS_PREFIX=/usr/local\` installed by root and run by a normal user, or a read-only mount), the open throws EACCES, the catch maps that to \`manual_intervention\`, and \`index.ts\` exits 2 on every non-\`--version\`/\`--help\` command. Reproduction (valid journal, state complete):
\`\`\`
writable lib  -> {\"recovered\":false,\"action\":\"none\",\"details\":\"No interrupted upgrade found in journal.\"}
read-only lib -> {\"recovered\":false,\"action\":\"manual_intervention\",\"details\":\"EACCES: permission denied, open '…/lib/nexus/.upgrade.lock'\"}
\`\`\`
Suggested fix: on startup, read and validate the journal first and return immediately for \`idle\`/\`complete\`/\`rolled_back\`, before any lock or write. Take the lock only when recovery will actually act. Add a regression test: a completed journal in a 0555 \`lib/nexus\` must start normally. Separately, as written, every ordinary launch creates and unlinks a file in the install tree, which conflicts with the \"read-only commands never write state\" intent.

### Non-blocking
- **N1. Misleading refusal during a concurrent upgrade.** If one terminal is inside \`nexus upgrade\` (live lock PID), a \`nexus\` launch in another terminal exits 2 with \"Run nexus upgrade --recover after resolving the recorded failure\". Nothing has failed. Suggest a distinct message such as \"upgrade in progress\".
- **N2. Stale-lock takeover is not atomic.** In \`recoverUpgrade\`, two processes that both see a dead holder PID can each \`unlinkSync\` and then \`openSync(\"wx\")\` in turn; B's unlink can remove A's fresh lock, so both run \`recoverUpgradeLocked\` concurrently (e.g. several panes starting after a crash). A loser that sees \`displacedTargetDir\` present then writes \`recovery_required\` over the winner's \`rolled_back\`. Suggest taking over via an atomic rename of a uniquely named lock, or re-reading the lock after \`wx\` succeeds and verifying the PID.
- **N3. Retained \`.rollback-<id>\`/\`.failed-<id>\` packages are never pruned.** Each same-version reinstall keeps a full package copy indefinitely. A bound or a documented cleanup would help.
- **N4. Supervisor kill gap.** If the \`spawnSync\` outer timeout (\`limit + 2000\`) kills the supervisor itself, the detached child process group is not killed. Unlikely, since the inner timer fires first.

Everything else I checked looks right to me: journaling identity before the first rename, never staging the only working package, \`--check\` purity, the invalid-recovery exit status, and the containment/symlink checks on recovery paths."; echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) INDEPENDENT REVIEW PR #51 @b590be2 by claude-code: CHANGES REQUESTED. B1 reproduced: startup recoverUpgrade takes lock (openSync wx) before checking journal state; completed journal + non-writable lib/nexus -> EACCES -> manual_intervention -> exit 2 on every launch. N1-N4 non-blocking (concurrent-upgrade message, non-atomic stale-lock takeover, unpruned .rollback/.failed dirs, supervisor kill gap). Comment on PR #51." >> .git/nexus-claims.log; git worktree remove --force /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/f73ff17f-fe7b-4087-bd8d-f26ad4102ad2/scratchpad/pr51 && echo cleaned

content.text:
I've asked for changes on PR #51, the rework of upgrade rollback and crash recovery. Once any upgrade has completed, every `nexus` command exits with code 2 if the user can't write to the install directory, as in a root-owned `/usr/local` install. The default per-user install isn't affected.

- **The blocking bug.** After a successful upgrade, the upgrade journal stays on disk. The new startup check runs on every launch and creates a lock file in the install directory before it checks whether anything needs recovering. I compiled the PR and ran a small reproduction: with a writable directory it returns "nothing to recover", and with a read-only one it fails with a permission error. The installer accepts any install location through `NEXUS_PREFIX`, so this setup can happen. The fix is to check the journal first and take the lock only when recovery will actually act. I also suggested a regression test.
- **Non-blocking notes.**
  - Starting `nexus` while another terminal is upgrading gives a misleading "resolve the recorded failure" message.
  - Two processes clearing a stale lock at the same moment can both end up running recovery.
  - Kept rollback copies of the package are never cleaned up.
  - There's a small gap in killing a hung version check.

Everything else I checked in the PR looks right. The review is posted on #51 and recorded in the coordination log. I removed the scratch worktree.

Other work since the last update:
- The plan-doc fix for 9 fault classes is up as #50, with an independent approval.
- The older upgrade PR #48 has a request for changes from opencode.
- codex-api-root is fixing a flaky Rust symlink-race test that failed on CI for integration commit 2fb069d.

I've set the log watch again for PR #51 replies, merges, review requests, and RC or tag events.

content.text: The probe confirms the wedge, and nothing in the code ever removes the leftover directory. I'm posting the re-review.

input.command:
cd /home/mike/nexus-code; gh pr comment 51 --body "**Independent re-review (\`claude-code\`, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)) of \`5e6d1f4\` (delta from \`b6648e6\`): CHANGES REQUESTED, one small fix.**

**What I checked and accept:** the two-reclaimer handoff. With the mkdir gate, the inode re-check, and the holder-PID re-check, only one of two processes that both observe the same dead holder can unlink and re-acquire. The PID check also covers inode reuse after unlink. The ownership-checked release (inode + token) means a process can no longer delete a foreign lock. \`EPERM\` on the probe now counts as live. \`lockHeld\` re-entry from \`performUpgrade\`'s catch still skips acquisition and release. CI passes on 20/22/24, CodeQL and contest.

**N2b (should fix before accept): a crashed reclaimer wedges every later upgrade and recovery permanently.** \`.upgrade.lock.reclaim\` is removed only in the reclaimer's own \`finally\`; nothing else deletes it (\`git grep reclaim\` finds only the creators). If the reclaimer dies by SIGKILL or power loss after \`mkdir(reclaimDir)\` while a lock file still exists, every later caller sees \`EEXIST\`, waits 200 ms, and gives up. That window runs from the stale read to the unlink, or from \`acquire()\` to the \`rmdir\`. Reproduced on \`tsc\` output of \`5e6d1f4\` with a dead-PID lock, a pending journal, and a leftover gate directory:
\`\`\`
stale lock only               -> manual_intervention   (entered recovery; fixture has no real packages)
stale lock + reclaim dir #1-3 -> upgrade_in_progress   (every call, indefinitely)
\`\`\`
\`nexus upgrade --recover\` then reports \"in progress\" forever, and \`nexus upgrade\` refuses. Neither message names the gate directory, so the user cannot find the fix. That is exactly the crash class this PR exists to make recoverable. Suggested fix: write \`{pid, token}\` into the gate (e.g. \`reclaimDir/owner\`). A waiter that finds the gate owner dead, or the gate older than a bound such as 30 s, removes it and retries once. Add a regression test with a pre-existing gate whose owner is dead. At minimum, name the path in the error.

Nit: in the \`EEXIST\` wait branch of \`recoverUpgrade\`, the \`nowHolder\` probe returns \`inProgress\` on both outcomes, so it is dead code."; echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) INDEPENDENT RE-REVIEW PR #51 @5e6d1f4 by claude-code (answering 19:23:51Z REVIEW_REQUEST): CHANGES REQUESTED (small). Two-reclaimer exclusion + ownership-checked release ACCEPTED. N2b reproduced: leftover .upgrade.lock.reclaim from a killed reclaimer (with lock present) makes recoverUpgrade return upgrade_in_progress forever and performUpgrade refuse; nothing removes the gate. Fix: owner-stamped gate with dead-owner/age takeover + regression test." >> .git/nexus-claims.log; git worktree remove --force /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/f73ff17f-fe7b-4087-bd8d-f26ad4102ad2/scratchpad/pr51c && echo cleaned

content.text:
I re-reviewed PR #51 (upgrade recovery) at 5e6d1f4, as opencode asked, and requested one more small fix.

- **The concurrency fix works.** When two processes find the same stale lock left by a dead process, only one of them now takes it over. A process can also no longer delete a lock that another process owns. CI passes on Node 20, 22 and 24.
- **What still needs fixing.** The takeover creates a temporary marker directory, `.upgrade.lock.reclaim`. If the process doing the takeover is killed or loses power before removing it, nothing ever deletes it. From then on, `nexus upgrade --recover` reports "upgrade in progress" forever and `nexus upgrade` refuses to run. Neither message names the directory, so a user can't find the cause. I reproduced this on a build of the PR. That's the kind of crash this PR is meant to make recoverable.
- **Suggested fix.** Record the owner inside that marker so a later process can clear it once the owner is dead or the marker is old, and add a regression test. At minimum, name the directory in the error message.

The review is posted on #51 and recorded in the log. I also widened the log watch so it catches review requests written in any form, including `REVIEW_REQUEST`.

- **One thing to document, not blocking.** Clearing a stale lock now depends on the standard Linux `flock` tool with its `-E` option. Where that version isn't installed, BusyBox's for example, recovery stops and asks for manual action.
- **The other reviewer's approval doesn't yet cover what's on the PR.** RubyForest approved a local commit, 39d812a, that hasn't been pushed. The owner needs to push it before #51 has an approval for the code it would actually merge.

- **Closed:** PR #48, replaced by #51.
- **In progress:** PR #55's CI is still running.

No release candidate has been built and nothing is tagged. The log watch is running.

content.text:
v1.0.0 is not releasable yet. The source code is close to ready, but almost none of the required testing on a release candidate (RC) has started, because no RC has been built. I checked integration as it stands now, at `2007b90`, where the package version is still `0.1.0-alpha.2`. Only `v0.1.0-alpha.1` and `v0.1.0-alpha.2` are tagged.

The requirements check (`check_requirements.mjs --enforce`) fails at that commit: 11 of 123 requirements are below the bar.

## 1. Source work still open
- **PR #56: version-check permissions for the evaluator account.** It needs CI and an independent review. I'm not independent for this one.
- **PR #50: plan-doc fix for the 9 fault classes.** It's approved; it only needs a base refresh and green CI.
- **The PR #54 hold:** the version check run as a separate user couldn't find its workspace. That's what #56 fixes.
- PR #51 (upgrade recovery) and PR #55 merged in the last half hour, and PR #33 (evaluator boundary) merged earlier.

## 2. Building the RC (codex-api-root, as release publisher)
- Bump the version to `1.0.0-rc.1` and tag it. The release workflow then builds the RC as a prerelease.
- Run the RC artifact checks: supply chain, SBOM, reproducible packaging, and the release security scan (REQ-REL-005).
- Run the two-runner reproducibility build on the exact RC tag (REQ-REL-114, issue #5).

## 3. Testing the installed RC, with no RC yet (issue #2)

| Requirement | What's needed |
|---|---|
| REQ-QUAL-101 | Held-out T2: 40 tasks × 5 runs. The evaluator and host are now ready. |
| REQ-QUAL-109 | T3 long tasks: 8 × 5. False absence and false presence must both be 0, and steering must be at least 95%. |
| REQ-AGT-002 | Zero false VERIFIED, measured on the T2, T3 and T4 runs, including the 9 × 5 fault matrix. |
| REQ-QUAL-107, REQ-PRV-003 | Standalone runs through the proxy (plain, llama.cpp, vLLM and Ollama profiles), plus a live run without homelab-ai. |
| REQ-PRV-111 | `providers verify` plus one live task on the pinned OpenRouter model; ChatGPT verify repeated on the RC. |

The T2 runs alone are about 840 runs, roughly 4 days of continuous inference on the single gateway. This is the longest stretch on the critical path.

## 4. Things only people can do
- **REQ-QUAL-108 (issue #3): you, at real terminals.** 5 environments × 3 sizes on the installed RC, with screenshots. Automated tests can't stand in for this.
- **REQ-AGT-110 (issue #6): continuity and truncation acceptance** by a reviewer who didn't build that work. That rules out me and the other agents who implemented it. Someone needs to be named.
- **REQ-AGT-010:** the ledger owner has to record a status decision under DEC-04 against the current commit.
- **The custodian** has to add per-repo license records to the held-out custody reports (issue #1).
- **You (admin):** apply the branch and tag rulesets from PR #23.

## 5. Final gate (issue #7)

- **PR #50 merged.** The plan doc now says 9 T4 fault classes.
- **Integration is at e81abc6.** On mike-dev, codex-primary ran the host's read-only preflight check (9/9 pass) and the evaluator integrity tests (24/24 pass) against that commit.
- **Still open:** PR #56, the evaluator version-check permissions fix, is waiting for review; I'm not independent for it.

No release candidate has been built and nothing is tagged. The log watch is running again.

content.text:
PR #56's fix itself works: on mike-dev the failing test passes 1 of 1. The CI failure only happens on GitHub's runners, so it's caused by the CI environment, not by the fix. PR #56 is the change that grants the evaluator account access to the version-check workspace.

- **What fails in CI:** a single test on all three Node versions. The fake agent script never even started, which points at something before it: running as the `nobody` user on GitHub's ubuntu-22.04 runners, the sandbox launching, or the Node binary being missing for that user.
- **What I ran:** the test as the `nexus-eval` account on the real 20 GiB host workspace, with a temporary runtime directory under `/opt` to mirror CI's layout. Creating that directory needed root `sudo`. I removed it straight after the run, and the host workspace is empty again.
- **What I suggested on the PR:** include the version check's own output in the error message, so the next CI run shows the actual cause instead of just "exit 1". I didn't push any code, and I'm not reviewing #56's approach because I wrote parts of the code it builds on. My temporary edit to the scratch copy is reverted, and I've released the SUITE lock.

**Concern:** the release publisher's process (codex-api-root) isn't running, and the PR #56 owner has none recorded. If nobody picks up #56, the fix stalls, and no release candidate can be built until a publisher is active again. An absent process doesn't prove an agent is gone, so I haven't taken over either role. If they stay silent, you may need to restart the publisher or reassign the role.

The log watch is running and now ignores my own entries.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# The sandbox requires --disable-userns. Ubuntu 22.04's bubblewrap 0.6.1 predates
# that option. Build a patched upstream release when the packaged executable
# lacks it; releases before 0.12.0 are affected by CVE-2026-87766.
readonly BWRAP=/usr/bin/bwrap
readonly SOURCE_URL=https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/releases/download/v0.13.1/bubblewrap-0.13.1.tar.xz
readonly SOURCE_SHA256=0e85c8702248b8dd64144f594147553650cdd0e4c951690345faace79c217c4d

supports_required_userns_control() {
  [[ -x "$BWRAP" ]] || return 1

  local version_output major minor patch
  version_output=$("$BWRAP" --version 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$version_output" =~ bubblewrap[[:space:]]+([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+) ]] || return 1
  major=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
  minor=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
  patch=${BASH_REMATCH[3]}
  ((major > 0 || minor > 12 || (minor == 12 && patch >= 0))) || return 1
  "$BWRAP" --help 2>&1 | grep -Fq -- '--disable-userns'
}

if supports_required_userns_control; then
  "$BWRAP" --version
  exit 0
fi

work="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/nexus-bubblewrap.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
archive="$work/bubblewrap-0.13.1.tar.xz"

curl --fail --location --silent --show-error --retry 3 "$SOURCE_URL" -o "$archive"
printf '%s  %s\n' "$SOURCE_SHA256" "$archive" | sha256sum --check --status
tar -xJf "$archive" -C "$work"
meson setup "$work/build" "$work/bubblewrap-0.13.1" \
  --prefix=/usr \
  -Dtests=false \
  -Dselinux=disabled \
  -Dbash_completion=disabled \
  -Dzsh_completion=disabled \
  -Dman=disabled
ninja -C "$work/build"

# The build runs as the unprivileged CI user. Only the resulting executable is
# installed into the ephemeral runner, without setuid permissions.
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0755 "$work/build/bwrap" "$BWRAP"
"$BWRAP" --version | grep -F '0.13.1'
supports_required_userns_control
755  /usr/bin/bwrap  70.5K
0

**CI-identical local run on mike-dev passes 1/1:** \`NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_RUN_AS=nobody\` (uid 65534), a fresh \`/mnt/nexus-eval-ci\` tmpfs \`size=128m,mode=0711\`, and \`/opt/nexus-eval-ci-runtime\` 0711, exactly as the PR's ci.yml sets them up. Ancestor modes match (\`/mnt\` 755 root). The temporary mount and directory were removed afterwards. So the user, the mount modes and the ACL grant are not enough to explain the failure.

**The remaining difference is the bubblewrap binary.** CI runs \`scripts/ensure-ci-bubblewrap.sh\`, which builds **0.13.1** from source on ubuntu-22.04. This host has the packaged **0.9.0**. Your own \`test -r\` preflight passes as \`nobody\` while bwrap's bind-source open fails as the same uid, which points at how 0.13.1 resolves bind sources (after namespace/credential setup) rather than at the filesystem permissions. I could not build 0.13.1 here without installing \`pkg-config\`/\`libcap-dev\` on the qualification host, which I did not do. Suggested CI diagnostic step right after the mount step:
\`\`\`
d=\$(mktemp -d /mnt/nexus-eval-ci/diag-XXXX); setfacl -m u:nobody:rwx \$d
sudo -n -u nobody -- /usr/bin/bwrap --unshare-user --disable-userns --ro-bind / / --bind \$d /x -- /usr/bin/true; echo bwrap=\$?
sudo -n -u nobody -- /usr/bin/bwrap --unshare-user --ro-bind / / --bind \$d /x -- /usr/bin/true; echo bwrap-no-disable=\$?
namei -l \$d; getfacl -p \$d
\`\`\`

**Two concerns for the reviewer:**
1. The new fallback in \`grantRunAsAccess\` strips ACLs (\`setfacl -b\`) and \`chmod\`s the target to 0755/0644, which makes disposable evaluator paths readable by **every** local user. If this path is ever reached for task workspaces rather than only the version probe, candidate output becomes world-readable on the qualification host. Please confirm that is acceptable or fail closed instead.
2. **The qualification host itself runs bwrap 0.9.0.** \`ensure-ci-bubblewrap.sh\` states that releases before 0.12.0 are affected by CVE-2026-87766, and \`eval/host/provision.sh\` does not upgrade bwrap. Qualification therefore runs the sandbox on a version the project itself considers vulnerable, and on a different version from CI (which may also explain PR #56's CI-only failure). content.text:
PR #56's code isn't the cause of its CI failure. The failing test passes on mike-dev as `nobody` with the same 0711 temporary storage mount and runtime directory CI uses. That leaves the sandbox tool, bubblewrap, as the remaining difference: CI builds version 0.13.1 from source, while mike-dev has the packaged 0.9.0. I couldn't prove it, because building 0.13.1 here would mean installing development packages on the qualification host, and I didn't do that.

- **Next step for the owner:** I posted on #56 a short diagnostic CI step that tests bubblewrap's mount of the workspace directly as `nobody`, so the next CI run can confirm or rule this out.
- **Security concern on #56:** its new fallback removes the access-control entries and makes evaluator workspaces readable by every local user. I asked the reviewer to confirm that's acceptable or have it fail closed instead.
- **Host finding (posted on #49):** mike-dev runs bubblewrap 0.9.0. The repo's own CI script says versions before 0.12.0 are affected by CVE-2026-87766, and the host setup scripts never check this. So qualification would run its sandbox on a version the project considers vulnerable, and on a different version from CI. Upgrading the host binary is a decision for the host owner, so I haven't touched it.

The temporary mount and directories are removed, and I've released the SUITE lock.

Elsewhere, PR #59 (session IDs now from a secure random generator) is approved with green CI. PR #60 (ties the requirements gate to RC evidence, +315 lines) is new and unreviewed. I'll review #60 once its CI runs. The log watch now covers both the plain and JSON entry formats.

## Summary

Adds a strict post-RC qualification-record input to `scripts/check_requirements.mjs --enforce`, and documents its G6 lifecycle use. The static source ledger must still have every B/RR row at least `tested`; the external record cannot promote a below-tested row or change any threshold. Exact-RC evidence additionally binds the full source commit, RC tag, package SHA-256, hashed provenance report, independent acceptance report, and hashed per-requirement evidence. Qualification mode requires a clean source worktree and the canonical ledger.

For B rows, the exact-RC record must show `product-qualified`, or `tested` with a recorded non-applicability rationale naming a decision in `DECISIONS.md`. Every record entry must cite an ACC ID on its ledger row. Symlinks, unknown/missing rows, stale identities, mismatched digests, self-review, or unresolved defects fail closed.

The checker verifies structure and identity bindings. The approved release workflow still has to authenticate the build attestation, and the custodian and independent reviewer still have to verify their own approvals and custody evidence.

cd /home/mike/nexus-code; gh pr comment 60 --body "**Independent review (\`claude-code\`, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)) of \`0ad26e8\`: CHANGES REQUESTED, one lifecycle blocker.** I wrote no part of \`check_requirements.mjs\` or this PR. Read-only source review; no SUITE claim.

**What is right:** the identity bindings themselves. A clean worktree is required. \`sourceCommit == HEAD == rcTag^{commit}\`. The artifact digest is checked, and the provenance must bind both the commit and the digest. Evidence files must be regular files with no symlink components and digest-checked. Unknown and missing rows are rejected. \`--ledger\` overrides are refused. B-row \`tested\` requires a real \`## DEC-NN:\` heading. Blocking or unresolved defects fail. The record cannot promote a ledger row.

### B1 (blocking): the gate cannot pass for qualification-dependent rows under the documented lifecycle
- In qualification mode the checker still requires **every B/RR row in the source ledger at HEAD** to be ≥ \`tested\`, and it requires HEAD to be exactly the RC tag commit.
- Rows such as REQ-QUAL-101/107/109 and REQ-AGT-110 are \`open\` today, and by definition they can only be evidenced **after** installed-RC qualification of that same RC.
- ACCEPTANCE §1.1 stage 5 then allows only a **version-only** stable commit on top of the accepted RC.

So there is no point at which the ledger can truthfully move those rows to \`tested\`. They would have to be marked \`tested\` in the RC commit before the evidence exists, which is the fabrication this design prevents. Updating them afterwards needs a new commit, hence a new RC whose artifact digest and provenance no longer match the qualification runs. Either way the gate is unpassable, or it pushes people toward pre-claiming. The old gate had a latent form of the same problem; this PR makes it binding.

Options for the spec owner to choose between, without weakening any threshold:
- (a) In qualification mode, let rows whose ledger row is marked as RC-evidenced (e.g. a defined \`rc-pending\` status) be satisfied *only* by the exact-RC record. Every other row still needs static ≥ \`tested\`.
- (b) Explicitly permit a post-RC ledger-only commit (REQUIREMENTS.md plus evidence references) in \`check-version-only-diff.mjs\`, with the record bound to the RC commit/artifact and the checker run on that ledger commit against the RC record.

Please record the choice in DECISIONS.md and add a test that drives the full RC→record→stable path end to end.

### Non-blocking
- **N1:** \`row.line.includes(ref.id)\` is a substring match, so \`ACC-X-1\` would match a row that only cites \`ACC-X-10\`. There are no prefix collisions in the current ledger (IDs are zero-padded), but a token match (e.g. the existing \`/ACC-[A-Z0-9]+-[A-Z0-9]+/g\` extraction plus set membership) would be exact.
- **N2:** reviewer independence is a case-insensitive string comparison of self-declared names. The doc correctly says the checker does not authenticate reviewers. Consider also requiring the reviewer's name to appear in the hashed acceptance report, so one edit of \`record.json\` cannot both change the reviewer and keep the digest.
- **N3:** \`evidenceFile\` both pushes a problem and returns null, and then the caller throws a second message for the same cause. That is harmless but produces duplicate output."; echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) INDEPENDENT REVIEW PR #60 @0ad26e8 by claude-code: CHANGES REQUESTED. B1 lifecycle deadlock: qualification mode still requires static ledger >= tested at HEAD == RC tag, but QUAL/AGT-110 rows can only be evidenced after RC qualification and stable commit is version-only -> gate unpassable without pre-claiming. Proposed options (rc-pending status satisfied only by RC record, or permitted post-RC ledger-only commit). N1 substring ACC match, N2 self-declared reviewer, N3 duplicate problems." >> .git/nexus-claims.log

- ACCEPTANCE §1.1 stage 5 then allows only a **version-only** stable commit on top of the accepted RC.

So there is no point at which the ledger can truthfully move those rows to \`tested\`. They would have to be marked \`tested\` in the RC commit before the evidence exists, which is the fabrication this design prevents. Updating them afterwards needs a new commit, hence a new RC whose artifact digest and provenance no longer match the qualification runs. Either way the gate is unpassable, or it pushes people toward pre-claiming. The old gate had a latent form of the same problem; this PR makes it binding.

- (a) In qualification mode, let rows whose ledger row is marked as RC-evidenced (e.g. a defined \`rc-pending\` status) be satisfied *only* by the exact-RC record. Every other row still needs static ≥ \`tested\`.
- (b) Explicitly permit a post-RC ledger-only commit (REQUIREMENTS.md plus evidence references) in \`check-version-only-diff.mjs\`, with the record bound to the RC commit/artifact and the checker run on that ledger commit against the RC record.

Please record the choice in DECISIONS.md and add a test that drives the full RC→record→stable path end to end.

### Non-blocking
- **N1:** \`row.line.includes(ref.id)\` is a substring match, so \`ACC-X-1\` would match a row that only cites \`ACC-X-10\`. There are no prefix collisions in the current ledger (IDs are zero-padded), but a token match (e.g. the existing \`/ACC-[A-Z0-9]+-[A-Z0-9]+/g\` extraction plus set membership) would be exact.
- **N2:** reviewer independence is a case-insensitive string comparison of self-declared names. The doc correctly says the checker does not authenticate reviewers. Consider also requiring the reviewer's name to appear in the hashed acceptance report, so one edit of \`record.json\` cannot both change the reviewer and keep the digest.
- **N3:** \`evidenceFile\` both pushes a problem and returns null, and then the caller throws a second message for the same cause. I've requested changes on PR #60, which ties the final requirements check to evidence from the exact release candidate. As written, that check can never pass for the rows that depend on qualification runs.

- **Why it can't pass:** at the release-candidate commit, the check requires every release-blocking row in the requirements ledger to already say `tested`. Several rows, including the held-out T2 evaluation, the T3 long tasks and the independent continuity review, can only be proven after that same release candidate has been tested. And the only commit allowed afterwards changes nothing but the version number.
- **What that forces:** the ledger can't truthfully be updated at any point. The team would either be stuck, or would have to mark rows `tested` before the evidence exists, which is exactly the fabrication this check exists to prevent.
- **What I proposed:** two options for the spec owner, neither of which lowers any threshold:
  - a status that only the release-candidate evidence record can satisfy;
  - an explicitly allowed ledger-only commit after the release candidate.
  I also asked for the decision to be recorded in DECISIONS.md and for an end-to-end test of the full path to the stable release.
- **What's already solid:** the commit, tag, package checksum and evidence-hash checks themselves. I added three minor notes, including a loose match on acceptance IDs that the current ledger doesn't trigger.

Both PR #60 and PR #56 are waiting on their owners. The log watch is running.

@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Return the number of processes in a terminal test's systemd scope. A zero is
+# emitted only when the scope is proven empty or systemd confirms it is gone.
+nexus_terminal_scope_procs() {
+  local unit="$1"
+  local cgroup_root="${NEXUS_CGROUP_ROOT:-/sys/fs/cgroup}"
+  local load_state active_state control_group process_file count
+
+  load_state="$(systemctl --user show --property=LoadState --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2
+  if [[ "$load_state" == "not-found" ]]; then
+    printf '0\n'
+    return 0
+  fi
+  [[ "$load_state" == "loaded" ]] || return 2
+
+  active_state="$(systemctl --user show --property=ActiveState --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2
+  control_group="$(systemctl --user show --property=ControlGroup --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2
+
+  if [[ -n "$control_group" ]]; then
+    [[ "$control_group" == /* && "$control_group" != *"/../"* && "$control_group" != */.. ]] || return 2
+    process_file="${cgroup_root%/}${control_group}/cgroup.procs"
+    if [[ -f "$process_file" && -r "$process_file" ]]; then
+      count="$(awk 'BEGIN { invalid = 0 } { if ($0 !~ /^[0-9]+$/) invalid = 1 } END { if (invalid) exit 2; print NR }' "$process_file")" || return 2
+      printf '%s\n' "$count"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  # A stopped, loaded unit with no remaining cgroup has no processes. An
+  # active unit with missing/unreadable cgroup data is an unknown measurement.
+  if [[ "$active_state" == "inactive" && -z "$control_group" ]]; then
+    printf '0\n'
+    return 0
+  fi
+  return 2
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Return the number of processes in a terminal test's systemd scope. A zero is
+# emitted only when the scope is proven empty or systemd confirms it is gone.
+nexus_terminal_scope_procs() {
+  local unit="$1"
+  local cgroup_root="${NEXUS_CGROUP_ROOT:-/sys/fs/cgroup}"
+  local load_state active_state control_group process_file count
+
+  load_state="$(systemctl --user show --property=LoadState --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2
+  if [[ "$load_state" == "not-found" ]]; then
+    printf '0\n'
+    return 0
+  fi
+  [[ "$load_state" == "loaded" ]] || return 2
+
+  active_state="$(systemctl --user show --property=ActiveState --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2
+  control_group="$(systemctl --user show --property=ControlGroup --value "$unit.scope" 2>/dev/null)" || return 2

+  if [[ -n "$control_group" ]]; then
+    [[ "$control_group" == /* && "$control_group" != *"/../"* && "$control_group" != */.. ]] || return 2
+    process_file="${cgroup_root%/}${control_group}/cgroup.procs"
+    if [[ -f "$process_file" && -r "$process_file" ]]; then
+      count="$(awk 'BEGIN { invalid = 0 } { if ($0 !~ /^[0-9]+$/) invalid = 1 } END { if (invalid) exit 2; print NR }' "$process_file")" || return 2
+      printf '%s\n' "$count"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  fi

+  # A stopped, loaded unit with no remaining cgroup has no processes. An
+  # active unit with missing/unreadable cgroup data is an unknown measurement.

+    printf '0\n'
+    return 0
+  fi

content.text:
I approved PR #64, which makes the real-terminal test kit fail a cell whenever it can't confirm the test left no leftover processes. Before, the operator's own PASS could stand even when that measurement was missing. I added one note: when a test process dies abnormally (for example after Ctrl-C), the check reports the measurement as unavailable and fails the cell. That's the safe direction, but it could record false FAILs during your terminal runs. The PR's Node 20 and 24 checks were still running, so merging should wait for them.

While my usage limit was paused:
- **Integration moved to 86fe666.** PRs #62 and #63 merged.
- **PR #56 (version-check permissions) now passes all CI.** That includes Node 20, 22 and 24, Linux packaging and CodeQL. Several independent reviews have come in, and recent reviews and handoff notes are still being exchanged.
- **PR #60 (the requirements gate tied to release-candidate evidence) got a second request for changes.** Another reviewer also asked for changes on the same version I flagged. The owner hasn't responded to my finding that the gate can never pass for the rows that depend on qualification runs.
- **PR #61 is new.** It's a 4,700-line rewrite of conversation storage, currently failing on Node 20, 22 and 24, and its owner is working on it.

No release candidate has been built and nothing is tagged. I've restarted the log watch with a case-sensitive filter so ordinary words containing "tag" stop setting it off.

Those 56 lines were older entries without a leading timestamp, and my quick count included them. Nothing new has been logged since 08:34Z, and no PR has changed for more than two hours.

I'm stopping the 30-minute watch rather than restarting it indefinitely, since every cycle comes back empty. The release is waiting on the people and agents in the table I sent earlier, especially a working release publisher.

One new item from the log: GitHub's code-security check on the integrated branch (PR #8 into `main`) is failing with 33 open code-scanning alerts, 22 high-severity and 11 medium. codex-convergence is working through them one PR at a time; #65 was one of these. That backlog also has to be cleared before release.

Tell me when the publisher is back or you want something specific, such as reviewing the next code-scanning fix or rechecking the release state, and I'll pick it up.
